CHECK AGAINST DELIVERY EMBARGOED UNTIL DELIVERY
ADDRESS BY THE PRIME MINISTER
NATIONAL PRESS CLUB
CANBERRA 5 MARCH 1986
I THANK YOU MADAM PRESIDENT, AND THROUGH YOU, THE NATIONAL
PRESS CLUB, FOR THE OPPORTUNITY ONCE AGAIN, TO REPORT TO THE
PEOPLE OF AUSTRALIA THROUGH THIS MOST IMPORTANT FORUM.
THIS IS IN EVERY WAY AN APPROPRIATE PLACE AND OCCASION TO
MARK THE THIRD ANNIVERSARY OF MY GOVERNMENT'S ELECTION IN
THE PRESENCE OF SO MANY OF YOU WHO HAVE BEEN THE CHRONICLERS
OF THOSE THREE YEARS.
AND LET ME SAY AT ONCE IN THE SPIRIT OF THE OCCASION,
MAGNANIMOUS IN VICTORY YOU HAVE CARRIED OUT THE TASK
RESPONSIBLY, OBJECTIVELY, IMPARTIALLY AND, IT ALMOST GOES
WITHOUT SAYING, WITH TOTAL ACCURACY AT ALL TIMES.
HAVING SAID THAT, LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, I NOW PROCEED TO THE
TASK IN HAND.
I
IT IS NOT MY INTENTION TO GIVE A COMPREHENSIVE CATALOGUE OF
THE ACHIEVEMENTS OF THE PAST THREE YEARS. AND I'M SURE
YOU'LL BE RELIEVED TO HEAR THAT.
FAR MORE IMPORTANT IS WHAT CAN BE ACHIEVED IN THE NEXT THREE
YEARS, AND BEYOND WHERE AUSTRALIA IS HEADING AND THE
CHALLENGES WHICH FACE US NOT CHALLENGES FOR THE GOVERNMENT
ALONE, BUT CHALLENGES FOR US ALL, AS AUSTRALIA ENTERS ITS
THIRD CENTURY.
IN ONE SENSE, THE THREE YEARS FROM 5 MARCH 1983 HAVE BEEN
FOUNDATION YEARS.
THEY HAVE NOT BEEN ONLY YEARS OF ACHIEVEMENT IN THEMSELVES,
BUT YEARS IN WHICH MY COLLEAGUES AND I HAVE TRIED TO KEEP
FIRMLY IN VIEW THE LONGER TERM RESPONSIBILITY TO BUILD FOR
AUSTRALIA'S FUTURE TO BUILD A STRONGER ECONOMY AND A
FAIRER SOCIETY.
AT THE OUTSET, THERE IS A POINT OF SUPREME IMPORTANCE WHICH
I MUST EMPHASISE. IT IS ABSOLUTELY FUNDAMENTAL TO MY
PHILOSOPHY AND FUNDAMENTAL TO THE PHILOSOPHY OF THE PARTY
AND GOVERNMENT I LEAD. 
IT IS TRUE THAT FOR THE PAST THREE YEARS THE PROBLEMS OF
ECONOMIC MANAGEMENT HAVE BEEN AT THE FOREFRONT OF OUR
CONCERNS. THAT WAS INEVITABLE GIVEN OUR INHERITANCE OF AN
ECONOMY IN DEEP CRISIS ON 5 MARCH 1983.
IT IS TRUE THAT THE RESTORATION OF GROWTH AND THE CREATION
OF JOBS HAVE BEEN AMONG OUR MOST CONSPICUOUS SUCCESSES. AND
THE PURSUIT OF SOUND RESPONSIBLE ECONOMIC MANAGEMENT WILL
REMAIN DOMINANT IN OUR POLICY CONSIDERATION.
BUT I EMPHASISE THAT THE LONGER TERM OBJECTIVE OF OUR
ECONOMIIC POLICIES IS TO USE THE FRUITS OF GROWTH TO CREATE
NOT ONLY A MORE PROSPEROUS SOCIETY BUT A MORE EQUITABLE
SOCIETY.
AND THAT IS THE WIDER MEASURE BY WHICH OUR RECORD OF THE
PAST THREE YEARS AND OUR PERFORMANCE AS A LABOR GOVERNMENT
IN THE YEARS TO COME MUST ULTIMATELY BE JUDGED.
WE ARE CERTAINLY PREPARED TO BE JUDGED ON OUR ECONOMIC
MANAGEMENT AND OUR ECONOMIC ACHIEVEMENT.
WE WILL MORE THAN CHEERFULLY BE JUDGED ON OUR RECORD AND OUR
POLICIES AGAINST THE ALTERNATIVE THE DISASTERS THEY
WROUGHT AND THE DISASTERS THEY PROPOSE.
BUT THOSE ARE NOT THE ONLY STANDARDS BY WHICH WE WOULD
CHOOSE TO BE JUDGED. WE WISH ALSO TO BE JUDGED BY THE
STANDARDS OF ACHIEVEMENT WHICH OUR PHILOSOPHY, OUR
OBJECTIVES, OUR ASPIRATIONS SET FOR US AS A LABOR
GOVERNMENT. TO PUT IT IN SPORTING TERMS, WE WANT TO BE JUDGED ULTIMATELY
AGAINST OUR PERSONAL BEST THE BEST LABOR STANDARDS, THE
BEST LABOR TRADITIONS, THE BEST LABOR ASPIRATIONS.
I! HERE CAN BE NO DOUBT WHATSOEVER ABOUT THE GREATEST SINGLE
ACHIEVEMENT OF THE PAST THREE YEARS.
THREE YEARS AGO I MADE, ON BEHALF OF THE AUSTRALIAN LABOR
PARTY, A COMMITMENT TO THE CREATION OF 500,000 JOBS IN OUR
FIRST THREE YEARS. THAT WAS AS IMPORTANT AND FUNDAMENTAL AN
UNDERTAKING AS HAS EVER BEEN GIVEN BY ANY LABOR LEADER
SEEKING ELECTION.
WE HAVE IN FACT BETTERED OUR COMMITMENT. SINCE APRIL 1983,
OVER 600,000 NEW JOBS 608,300 TO BE PRECISE HAVE BEEN
CREATED IN AUSTRALIA.
AND I BELIEVE THAT'S A REAL CAUSE FOR CELEBRATION, NOT JUST
FOR A LABOR GOVERNMENT ON ITS THIRD ANNIVERSARY, BUT FOR ALL
AUSTRALIANS. BUT ALMOST AS IMPORTANT AS WHAT RAS BEEN ACHIEVED IS THE WAY
IT HAS BEEN ACHIEVED.
IT HAS NOT BEEN ACHIEVED BY SETTING OFF A NEW SPIRAL OF
INFLATION, BY GOING FOR EXCESSIVE FISCAL STIMULUS. 
ON THE CONTRARY, WE HAVE MORE THAN HALVED THE BUDGET DEFICIT
BEQUEATHED TO US BY OUR PREDECESSORS AND HAVE NOW SET
INFLATION FIRMLY ON A DOWNWARD PATH, DESPITE THE SIGNIFICANT
UPWARD PRESSURES STEMMING FROM LAST YEAR'S DEPRECIATION.
WE HAVE NOT BEEN IN THE BUSINESS OF PURCHASING TEMPORARY
POLITICAL GAIN AT THE EXPENSE OF OUR LONGER TERM ECONOMIC
AND SOCIAL OBJECTIVES.
FOR US, THE CREATION OF JOBS HAS NOT ONLY BEEN A CENTRAL
OBJECTIVE OF OUR ECONOMIC POLICIES, IT IS CENTRAL TO OUR
SOCIAL OBJECTIVES OUR OBJECTIVES OF GREATER EQUITY, NOT
ONLY FOR THOSE ABLE TO TAKE PART IN THE PRODUCTIVE PROCESSES
DIRECTLY, BUT FOR THOSE OF OUR FELLOW AUSTRALIANS WHO DEPEND
UPON A COMPASSIONATE SOCIETY IF THEY ARE TO SHARE EQUITABLY
IN THE FRUITS OF GROWTH.
UNEMPLOYMENT ITSELF IS ACKNOWLEDGED AS THE SINGLE MOST
IMPORTANT CAUSE OF POVERTY IN AUSTRALIA. CLEARLY,
UNEMPLOYMENT CAN BE LOWERED PERMANENTLY ONLY THROUGH
SUSTAINED ECONOMIC GROWTH.
SIMILARLY IT IS CLEAR THAT THE CAPACITY OF SOCIETY
PROGRESSIVELY TO REDISTRIBUTE INCOME IN FAVOUR OF THE
POOREST IS GREATER IN A GROWING ECONOMY. AND ECONOMIC
GROWTH CAN BE MAXIMISED ONLY THROUGH THE PURSUIT OF ECONOMIC
EFFICIENCY. I WANT TO DISPEL UTTERLY THE ILLUSION, FOSTERED SO
ASSIDUOUSLY, AND INSIDIOUSLY IN CERTAIN QUARTERS, THAT FOR A
LABOR GOVERNMENT, THE REQUIREMENTS OF SOUND ECONOMIC
MANAGEMENT AND OUR HIGHER SOCIAL OBJECTIVES ARE
INCOMPATIBLE. THERE IS NO CONFLICT BETWEEN EFFICIENCY AND EQUITY.
ON THE CONTRARY IN TODAY'S WORLD, IN TODAY'S ECONOMY, THERE
CAN BE NO EQUITY WITHOUT EFFICIENCY.
WHILE ECONOMIC EFFICIENCY CANNOT OF ITSELF GUARANTEE GREATER
EQUITY, IT IS CERTAINLY A NECESSARY CONDITION FOR THE
CREATION OF A FAIRER SOCIETY.
IT JUST STATES PART OF OUR CASE TO SAY THAT ONLY A LABOR
GOVERNMENT POSSESSES THE WILL TO PURSUE THE TWIN GOALS OF
EFFICIENCY AND EQUITY SIMULTANEOUSLY AS WE HAVE DONE FOR
THE PAST THREE YEARS.
CERTAINLY, GREATER EQUITY, A FAIRER SOCIETY, IS NOT AND HAS
NEVER BEEN ON THE AGENDA OF OUR OPPONENTS.
BUT NEITHER IS ECONOMIC EFFICIENCY.
FOR PROOF OF THAT, YOU DO NOT HAVE TO GO BACK TO THEIR
PERFORMANCE IN THE YEARS BEFORE 1983.
THEY HAVE MADE IT CLEAR, UNDER THEIR CURRENT LEADERSHIP,
THAT THEY ARE COMMITTED TO THE ABANDONMENT OF THE VERY 
CONDITIONS UPON WHICH THE ACHIEVEMENTS OF THE PAST THREE
YEARS HAVE BEEN SECURED, AND UPON WHICH THE NATION'S
PROSPECTS FOR SUSTAINED AND SUSTAINABLE GROWTH CHIEFLY REST.
A STRIKING PARADOX OF OUR AGE IS THAT THE CONSERVATIVES WHO
PROFESS SOME CONCERN FOR HISTORY APPEAR INCAPABLE OF EVER
LEARNING THE LESSONS OF HISTORY.
AND HISTORY SHOWS US CLEARLY THAT ECONOMIC PROGRESS IS
FASTEST WHEN THE COMMUNITY SHARES COMMON GOALS AND HAS
AGREED PRIORITIES.
THAT IS MOST LIKELY TO BE THE CASE WHEN ALL PARTICIPANTS ARE
SURE THAT THE FRUITS OF GROWTH ARE TO BE FAIRLY DISTRIBUTED.
FOR EXAMPLE, IT IS NOW WIDELY ACCEPTED THAT THE ECONOMIC
RECOVERIES OF THE SEVENTIES PROVED SHORT-LIVED, BECAUSE
DISPUTES OVER INCOME CLAIMS COULD ONLY BE RECONCILED AT THE
PRICE OF GROWTH-DESTROYING INFLATION.
FURTHER, IT IS ALSO PLAIN THAT PEOPLE ARE MORE WILLING TO
ACCEPT STRUCTURAL CHANGES WHICH COULD ADVERSELY AFFECT THEM
IN THE SHORT TERM, BUT WHICH ARE ULTIMATELY DIRECTED AT
PROMOTING ECONOMIC GROWTH, IF THEY BELIEVE THAT BENEFITS OF
THAT HIGHER GROWTH PERFORMANCE ARE TO BE SHARED EQUITABLY.
AND OF COURSE, OUR RECOGNITION OF THESE PRINCIPLES HAS BEEN
AT THE HEART OF OUR APPROACH FROM DAY ONE FROM THE DAY WE
SET ABOUT THE PROCESS OF NATIONAL RECONCILIATION, RECOVERY
AND RECONSTRUCTION.
IT IS AN APPROACH WHICH HAS FOUND ITS MOST EFFECTIVE
EXPRESSION IN THE ACCORD -NOT JUST THE DOCUMENT CALLED THE
PRICES AND INCOMES ACCORD -BUT IN ITS ACTUAL OPERATION.
THERE IS NOTHING MORE CURIOUS IN THE CURRENT POLITICAL SCENE
AND LET ME SAY, NOTHING MORE SPURIOUS THAN THE LINE
PEDDLED, CHIEFLY BUT NOT EXCLUSIVELY BY OUR OPPONENTS, THAT
THIS LABOR GOVERNMENT IS TOO CLOSE TO BUSINESS AND TOO CLOSE
TO THE UNIONS.
LET ME MAKE IT ABSOLUTELY CLEAR THAT I MAKE NO APOLOGY
WHATSOEVER FOR THE EXTENT TO WHICH WE HAVE BEEN ABLE TO
ESTABLISH WITH THE KEY ECONOMIC GROUPINGS IN THE COMMUNITY
AN UNPRECEDENTED LEVEL OF UNDERSTANDING ABOUT COMMON GOALS,
PRIORITIES AND PROBLEMS.
I MAKE NO APOLOGY FOR A PROCESS AND AN APPROACH THROUGH
WHICH 600,000 JOBS HAVE BEEN CREATED IN THREE YEARS.
I MAKE NO APOLOGY FOR A PROCESS WHICH HAS REDUCED INDUSTRIAL
DISPUTATION TO THE LOWEST LEVEL FOR SIXTEEN YEARS.
I MAKE NO APOLOGY FOR AN APPROACH WHICH HAS LED TO THE
RESTORATION OF THE PROFIT SHARE AND THE CORRESPONDING
DECLINE IN REAL UNIT LABOUR COSTS TO THE LEVELS OF THE LATE
1960' S AND EARLY 19701S.
I MAKE NO APOLOGY FOR THE FACT THAT OUR INTERNATIONAL 
COMPETITIVENESS HAS NOW BEEN RESTORED TO THE LEVELS OF
YEARS AGO AND THAT THAT IMPROVEMENT IS EXPECTED
SUBSTANTIALLY TO BE RETAINED OVER THE LIFE OF THE ACCORD
MARK II.
AND I MAKE NO APOLOGY FOR AN APPROACH WHICH HAS CREATED
THROUGHOUT THE COMMUNITY A NEW AWARENESS AND ACCEPTANCE OF
THE NEED FOR FUNDAMENTAL RESTRUCTURING OF KEY SECTORS OF THE
AUSTRALIAN ECONOMY, NOW UNDER WAY.
AND IF CLOSENESS MEANS OUR CAPACITY TO CONSULT AND
CO-OPERATE, TO AN EXTENT UNMATCHED BY ANY PREVIOUS
AUSTRALIAN GOVERNMENT, I MAKE NO APOLOGY FOR THAT EITHER.
THIS HAS BEEN AN APPROACH WHICH IS SERVING AUSTRALIA WELL.
IT MUST CONTINUE.
AND TWO THINGS HAVE TO BE UNDERSTOOD ABOUT THE ACCORD, IN
ITS WIDEST MEANING.
FIRST, IT PROVIDES A FRAMEWORK OF CERTAINTY AND
PREDICTABILITY, YET AT THE SAME TIME IT IS FLEXIBLE ENOUGH
TO COPE WITH UNFORESEEN CHANGES IN ECONOMIC CIRCUMSTANCES.
AND SECONDLY, THE ACCORD GOES FAR BEYOND BEING A UNIQUELY
SUCCESSFUL METHOD OF INCREASING EMPLOYMENT, REDUCING
INDUSTRIAL DISPUTATION AND CONTROLLING INFLATION. IT IS A
COMPLEX OF AGREEMENTS AND UNDERSTANDINGS ABOUT ECONOMIC AND
SOCIAL GOALS FOR THIS NATION THE GOALS WHICH ARE
FUNDAMENTAL TO THIS LABOR GOVERNMENT'S VISION FOR AUSTRALIA.
BUT WE COULD NOT HAVE MOVED SO FIRMLY AND SUCCESSFULLY
TOWARDS THE ACHIEVEMENT OF THOSE GOALS IF SUPPORT FOR THEM
HAD BEEN CONFINED TO THOSE GROUPS AND INTERESTS
TRADITIONALLY DEFINED AS LABOR.
WYEN WE UNDERTOOK THREE YEARS AGO TO TURN THE ECONOMY
AROUND, LABOR PRESENTED AUSTRALIA WITH A NEW APPROACH
DESIGNED TO ENLIST THE WIDEST POSSIBLE COMMUNITY SUPPORT.
THE ACCORD WAS PART OF THE APPROACH. SO WAS THE SUMMIT.
AND LET ME REMIND YOU THAT THE SUMMIT COMMUNIQUE REPRESENTED
WIDE AGREEMENT ON SOCIAL AS WELL AS ECONOMIC GOALS.
MANY COMMENTATORS WERE SCEPTICAL OF OUR APPROACH.
NOW OF COURSE NOBODY HERE WAS AMONG THE RANKS OF THE CYNICS.
IN PARTICULAR THERE WERE THOSE WHO WERE SCEPTICAL ABOUT THE
ABILITY OF THE ACCORD TO ENDURE AND TO SECURE SUSTAINED
GROWTH WITHOUT A RE-EMERGENCE OF UNCONTROLLED INFLATION.
THE RECORD SPEAKS FOR ITSELF. IT REPRESENTS A SUBSTANTIAL
DOWNPAYMENT ON OUR PROMISE TO DELIVER LONG-TERM GROWTH. BUT
A DOWNPAYMENT IS NOT ENOUGH. WE HAVE SET ABOUT CASTING
ASIDE THE MANY OBSTACLES TO GROWTH LEFT ALONG THE TRACK BY
PREVIOUS COALITION GOVERNMENTS. 
WE HAVE ENCOURAGED INDUSTRY AND COMMERCE TO BECOME MORE
ROBUST AND INTERNATIONALLY COMPETITIVE, MORE
EXPORT-ORIENTED, MORE WILLING TO SEEK OUT MARKET
OPPORTUNITIES, MORE READY TO TAKE ADVANTAGE OF DEVELOPMENTS
IN TECHNOLOGY AND MODERN BUSINESS PRACTICE, AND LESS RELIANT
ON GOVERNMENT ASSISTANCE AND INTERVENTION.
WAGE RESTRAINT THROUGH THE ACCORD, STRONG PRODUCTIVITY
GROWTH, AND THE SIGNIFICANT DEPRECIATION OF THE AUSTRALIAN
DOLLAR IN 1985, HAVE MADE OUR MANUFACTURING INDUSTRIES MORE
INTERNATIONALLY COMPETITIVE THAN THEY HAVE BEEN FOR AT LEAST
FIFTEEN YEARS.
AND IT IS HEARTENING TO SEE THAT THE MANUFACTURING SECTOR IS
RESPONDING TO THAT OPPORTUNITY. THERE IS FIRM EVIDENCE OF
INCREASING MANUFACTURING INVESTMENT AND RISING PRODUCTIVITY,
TOGETHER WITH GREATER TECHNOLOGICAL AWARENESS, AND A MORE
CO-OPERATIVE APPROACH BETWEEN EMPLOYERS, UNIONS AND
GOVERNMENT. THE GOVERNMENT'S CAREFULLY CO-ORDINATED, WIDE-RANGING
PROGRAM OF POLICY INITIATIVES FOR AUSTRALIAN INDUSTRY HAS
CONTRIBUTED IMPORTANTLY TO THIS NEW-FOUND VIGOUR.
IN PARTICULAR, THE GOVERNMENT HAS ESTABLISHED SPECIAL
SECTORAL PLANS FOR ADDRESSING THE PROBLEMS FACING CERTAIN
LARGE AND PREVIOUSLY AILING INDUSTRIES SUCH AS STEEL AND
MOTOR VEHICLES.
AND WE HAVE PROMOTED AN UPGRADING OF THE TECHNOLOGICAL
CAPACITY OF MANUFACTURING INDUSTRY BY BRINGING ABOUT A
SUBSTANTIAL INCREASE IN THE R D EFFORT OF PRIVATE
INDUSTRY, BETTER LINKING INDUSTRY TO THE PUBLIC RESEARCH
INSTITUTIONS, AND PROVIDING A BETTER BASIS FOR NEW PRODUCTS,
PROCESSES AND ENTERPRISES UPON WHICH FUTURE GROWTH DEPENDS.
I1 ADDITION WE HAVE ALREADY TAKEN SUBSTANTIAL STEPS TO
REMOVE UNNECESSARY OR OUTMODED REGULATIONS AND RESTRICTIONS
ESPECIALLY, BUT NOT EXCLUSIVELY, IN THE FINANCIAL SECTOR.
IN EACH CASE OUR OBJECTIVE HAS BEEN TO SECURE FOR AUSTRALIA
AN ENVIRONMENT WHICH WILL PERMIT AND ENCOURAGE EFFICIENT,
COMPETITIVE AUSTRALIAN INDUSTRIES TO CONTRIBUTE THEIR FULL
POTENTIAL TO INCREASING AND SUSTAINING ECONOMIC GROWTH IN
AUSTRALIA. THE SAME APPROACH HAS CHARACTERISED THE GOVERNMENT'S
RESPONSE TO THE DIFFICULTIES FACED BY THE RURAL SECTOR.
WE ARE SEEKING DOMESTICALLY TO MITIGATE THE IMPACT OF
ESCALATING FARM COSTS ON OUR RURAL PRODUCERS. THE RECENT
GOVERNMENT DECISION ON FUEL COSTS IS EVIDENCE OF THIS.
WE HAVE SOUGHT AT THE SAME TIME TO PROMOTE MORE EFFICIENT
M4ARKETING AND PRODUCTION PRACTICES WITHIN THE RURAL SECTOR.
THE REFORMS WE HAVE INTRODUCED IN PRIMARY INDUSTRY STATUTORY
M4ARKETING AUTHORITIES, AND THE PLANS WE HAVE DEVELOPED FOR
THE DAIRY AND SUGAR INDUSTRIES, TESTIFY TO OUR COMMITMENT TO 
SEEING AUSTRALIAN RURAL INDUSTRIES SURVIVE AND PROSPER.
FINALLY, WE ARE WORKING TO SECURE A REVERSAL OF THE POLICIES
OF OTHERS, WHICH ARE CORRUPTING INTERNATIONAL MARKETS.
DURING THE PERIOD WE HAVE BEEN IN OFFICE WE HAVE
CONSISTENTLY MADE CLEAR TO THE EEC OUR CONCERN ABOUT THE
DISASTROUS EFFECTS OF ITS COMMON AGRICULTURAL POLICY ON
WORLD TRADE IN AGRICULTURAL COMMODITIES. MORE RECENTLY WE
HAVE EXPRESSED OUR CONCERN TO SENIOR MEMBERS OF THE UNITED
STATES ADMINISTRATION AND CONGRESS ABOUT THE FURTHER ADVERSE
CONSEQUENCES FOR OUR RURAL PRODUCERS OF THEIR EXPORT
ENHANCEMENT PROGRAM.
IN EACH CASE THE GOVERNMENT HAS NOT HESITATED TO PUT ITS
VIEWS STRONGLY TO THE EEC AND THE UNITED STATES BECAUSE,
DESPITE OUR CLOSE FOREIGN POLICY AND HISTORICAL TIES WITH
THESE COUNTRIES, WE WILL NOT STAND IDLY BY WHILE THEIR
AGRICULTURAL POLICIES AND PROGRAMS DAMAGE OUR VITAL RURAL
SECTOR. I AM, THEREFORE, PLEASED TO ANNOUNCE TODAY THAT I HAVE
RECEIVED A POSITIVE RESPONSE FROM PRESIDENT REAGAN FOR AN
EARLY MEETING WITH HIM AND WITH OTHER SENIOR MEMBERS OF HIS
ADMINISTRATION. THEY HAVE SUGGESTED, AND WE HAVE AGREED,
THAT THESE MEETINGS SHOULD TAKE PLACE ON 17 APRIL. ON THIS
VISIT I WOULD ALSO EXPECT TO MEET WITH SENIOR CONGRESSIONAL
LEADERS. THESE MEETINGS IN WASHINGTON WILL DISCUSS WAYS OF ENSURING
THAT THE EXPORT ENHANCEMENT PROGRAM DOES NOT HAVE A NEGATIVE
IMPACT ON OUR RURAL SECTOR, AND HOW BEST TO PROMOTE A MORE
RATIONAL INTERNATIONAL TRADING SYSTEM IN AGRICULTURAL
PRODUCTS AT THE FORTHCOMING ECONOMIC SUMMIT OF THE HEADS OF
GOVERNMENT OF THE LEADING INDUSTRIALISED COUNTRIES.
14ADIES AND GENTLEMEN
AT THIS POINT I WISH TO REVERT TO MY BASIC THEME AND TO
EMPHASISE AGAIN THAT FOR THIS LABOR GOVERNMENT THE GOALS OF
GREATER EFFICIENCY AND GREATER EQUITY ARE INDISSOLUBLY
LINKED.
CENTRAL TO OUR POLICIES IS THE UNDERSTANDING THAT ONLY A
GROWING ECONOMY CAN FULFILL THE LEGITIMATE ASPIRATIONS OF
ALL AUSTRALIANS ENGAGED IN PRODUCTIVE ACTIVITY TO IMPROVED
LIVING STANDARDS AND A BETTER QUALITY OF LIFE.
BUT IT IS EQUALLY TRUE THAT AN EXPANDING ECONOMY CAN BEST
PROVIDE THE OPPORTUNITIES TO SATISFY ASPIRATIONS OF
AUSTRALIANS TO CARE FOR THE NEEDY AND THOSE LESS ABLE TO
CARE FOR THEMSELVES.
OUR WELFARE INITIATIVES HAVE CONCENTRATED ON THOSE IN
GREATEST NEED THE UNEMPLOYED, LOW INCOME FAMILIES WITH
CHILDREN AND SOCIAL SECURITY BENEFICIARIES RENTING
PRIVATELY. INDEED THE IMPACT OF THESE INITIATIVES HAS BEEN TO INCREASE 
THE REAL DISPOSABLE INCOME OF PEOPLE ON SOCIAL SECURITY BY
UP To 20 PER CENT SINCE 1983. DESPITE THE SHARP DROP IN
THEIR REAL INCOMES IN THE YEARS 1976-77 TO 1982-83, ALMOST
EVERYONE ON A FULL PENSION NOW HAS A HIGHER DISPOSABLE
INCOME THAN THEY DID A DECADE AGO, SOME BY UP TO 10 PER
CENT. A MORE GENERAL INDICATOR OF OUR WILLINGNESS TO RE-ORDER
PRIORITIES TO ASSIST THE NEEDY IS THE FACT THAT THE SHARE OF
COMMONWEALTH OUTLAYS ( EXCLUDING PUBLIC DEBT INTEREST)
DIRECTED TO HEALTH, WELFARE AND HOUSING HAS RISEN STEADILY
IN EACH OF OUR BUDGETS, AND IS NOW OVER 3 PERCENTAGE POINTS
HIGHER THAN IN THE 1982-83 BUDGET.
THE SWEEPING TAXATION REFORMS WE HAVE ANNOUNCED WILL ENHANCE
SOCIAL EQUITY THROUGH THE MEASURES TO REDUCE POVERTY TRAPS
AND THROUGH THE CLOSURE OF TAX SHELTERS. AND THE REFORMS
WILL CONTRIBUTE TO GROWTH BY PROVIDING GREATER INCENTIVE TO
UNDERTAKE PRODUCTIVE WORK.
OUR POLICIES IN THE CRITICAL FIELD OF EDUCATION ARE DIRECTED
TO IMPROVING THE QUALITY AND RELEVANCE OF EDUCATION,
ENSURING EQUALITY OF OPPORTUNITY AND ENCOURAGING STUDENTS TO
REMAIN LONGER IN EDUCATION AND TRAINING.
WE HAVE DONE SO IN RECOGNITION NOT ONLY OF THE MAJOR
ECONOMIC BENEFITS WHICH WOULD FLOW-FROM A MORE ADAPTABLE,
MORE HIGHLY SKILLED WORKFORCE BUT ALSO-IN RECOGNITION OF THE
INESTIMABLE VALUE TO INDIVIDUAL STUDENTS OF A MORE RELEVANT
EDUCATION. INDEED, A HIGH PRIORITY HAS BEEN ACCORDED TO INTRODUCING A
PHASED PROGRAM TO RATIONALISE AND ENHANCE YOUTH INCOME
SUPPORT ARRANGEMENTS TO ENSURE THAT OUR YOUNG PEOPLE HAVE
MORE INCENTIVE TO CONTINUE IN EDUCATION RATHER THAN OPT OUT
INFO. UNEMPLOYMENT.
THIS WAS PART OF A PACKAGE OF INTEGRATED MEASURES
IMPLEMENTED IN THE 1985-86 BUDGET PRIORITY ONE THAT
ESTABLISHED FOR THE FIRST TIME, A COHERENT SET OF POLICIES
AND PROGRAMS TO PROVIDE GREATLY ENHANCED OPPORTUNITIES FOR
YOUNG PEOPLE TO CONTINUE EDUCATION, TO ACQUIRE SKILLS AND TO
UNDERTAKE PRODUCTIVE EMPLOYMENT.
A CENTRAL ELEMENT OF PRIORITY ONE IS THE TRAINEESHIP SCHEME
WHICH WILL PROVIDE YOUNG PEOPLE WITH A MAJOR IMPROVEMENT IN
VOCATIONAL TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES AND ESPECIALLY IN THEIR
TRANSITION FROM SCHOOL TO WORK.
AND LET ME HERE MAKE THIS POINT AN ESSENTIAL ELEMENT IN
THE WORKING OF PRIORITY ONE IS THE NEED FOR UNIONS,
EMPLOYERS AND THE YOUNG PEOPLE THEMSELVES TO GET BEHIND
IT. IT IS A SPECIFIC EXAMPLE OF THE WAY IN WHICH IN THE
FINAL ANALYSIS, THE FULL SUCCESS OF OUR ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL
INITIATIVES REQUIRES COMMUNITY SUPPORT AND C0OMUNITY
CO-OPERATION, IN THE SPIRIT OF THE ACCORD ITSELF.
LADIES AND GENTLEMEN. 
A BALANCED ACCOUNT OF THE PAST THREE YEARS MUST, OF COURSE,
INCLUDE REFERENCE TO AUSTRALIA'S ENHANCED INTERNATIONAL
STANDING AS REFLECTED IN THE RECORD VOTE WE RECEIVED IN
1984 FOR OUR MEMBERSHIP OF THE UNITED NATIONS SECURITY
COUNCIL. WE HAVE TAKEN AS OUR GUIDING PRINCIPLES THE
IMPERATIVE OF AUSTRALIA'S INDEPENDENCE AND NATIONAL
SECURITY; THE ASPIRATIONS OF THE AUSTRALIAN PEOPLE TO LIVE
IN A WORLD FREE OF THE THREAT OF NUCLEAR WAR; AND THE
STRATEGIC AND ECONOMIC FACTS OF AUSTRALIA'S POSITION IN THE
ASIA-PACIFIC REGION.
FACED BY THE DIFFICULTIES IN THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN THE
UNITED STATES AND NEW ZEALAND, WE HAVE WORKED SUCCESSFULLY
TO ENSURE THE CONTINUING STRENGTH OF OUR SECURITY
ARRANGEMENTS WITH THE UNITED STATES UNDER ANZUS. AT THE
SAME TIME, WE HAVE STRIVEN TO ENSURE THAT OUR CLOSE
RELATIONSHIPS WITH NEW ZEALAND, INCLUDING THE DEFENCE
RELATIONSHIP, IS IN NO WAY DIMINISHED.
WE WILL CONTINUE TO MAKE WHATEVER CONSTRUCTIVE CONTRIBUTION
WE CAN TO ENCOURAGE THE RESTORATION OF TRILATERAL
CO-OPERATION UNDER ANZUS, AND AT ALL EVENTS TO ENSURE THAT
OUR TWO-WAY COMMITMENTS TO AND WITH THE UNITED STATES REMAIN
FULLY OPERABLE AND IN FORCE.
AUSTRALIA SHARED WITH MOST OTHER COUNTRIES AROUND THE WORLD
A GREAT SENSE OF RELIEF WHEN THE SUPER-POWERS RESUMED
SERIOUS NEGOTIATIONS ON ARMS CONTROL AND DISARMAMENT. WE
SHOULD NOT, HOWEVER, UNDERESTIMATE THE DIFFICULTIES WHICH
LIE ON THE PATH TO AGREEMENT. NOR SHALL WE IN ANY WAY RELAX
OUR OWN EFFORTS IN THIS AREA.
OUR MAJOR ACHIEVEMENT IN THE ARMS CONTROL AREA IS OUR
INITIATIVE TO DEVELOP THROUGH THE SOUTH PACIFIC FORUM THE
SOUTH PACIFIC NUCLEAR FREE ZONE TREATY. THE CONCLUSION OF
TIHE TREATY SIGNALS OUR DETERMINATION TO DO WHATEVER WE CAN
IN THE FIELD OF ARMS CONTROL. IT ALSO EXEMPLIFIES THE
PRIORITY WHICH WE HAVE GIVEN TO AUSTRALIA'S OWN PART OF THE
WORLD, THE ASIA-PACIFIC REGION.
FROM THE OUTSET OF ITS TIME IN OFFICE, THE GOVERNMENT HAS
INVESTED THE HIGHEST POSSIBLE ENERGY AND RESOURCES TO THE
DEVELOPMENT OF AUSTRALIA'S RELATIONS WITH ALL ITS
NEIGHBOURS. THE FRUITS OF THESE EFFORTS CAN BE SEEN IN MANY
WAYS. I WOULD MENTION ONLY ON THIS OCCASION THE CONSTRUCTIVE
DISCUSSIONS WHICH BILL HAYDEN HAS JUST HAD WITH INDONESIA
LEADERS ON A NUMBER OF SUBJECTS, INCLUDING THE SEA BED
BOUNDARY; THE DEVELOPMENT OF A COMPREHENSIVE RELATIONSHIP
W4ITH CHINA, WHICH I LOOK FORWARD TO VISITING AGAIN IN MAY;
AND OUR RESPONSE TO THE DEVELOPING SITUATION IN THE
PHILIPPINES, AS A RESULT OF WHICH I WOULD SUGGEST THAT NO
COUNTRY IS BETTER PLACED THAN AUSTRALIA TO ESTABLISH A
CO-OPERATIVE RELATIONSHIP WITH THE GOVERNMENT OF PRESIDENT
AQUINO. LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, 
IN THIS NECESSARILY VERY GENERAL ACCOUNT OF THE PAST THREE
YEARS I HAVE TRIED TO PLACE OUR ACHIEVEMENTS FIRMLY IN THE
CONTEXT OF OUR GOALS OF GREATER EFFICIENCY AND GREATER
EQUITY.
THIS DISCUSSION OF OUR ACHIEVEMENTS IS NOT TO DENY THAT IN
M4ANY RESPECTS THE KEY ECONOMIC DECISIONS WE MUST NOW MAKE
ARE MORE DIFFICULT AND COMPLEX THAN THOSE THAT FACED THE
GOVERNMENT IN 1983.
THE IMMEDIATE GOALS OF A GOVERNMENT ELECTED, AS WE WERE, TO
DEAL WITH THE WORST ECONOMIC CRISIS FOR FIFTY YEARS, WERE
RELATIVELY SIMPLE, ALTHOUGH THERE WAS CERTAINLY NOTHING
SIMPLE OR EASY-ABOUT THE MEANS BY WHICH THAT CRISIS COULD BE
BROUGHT TO AN END AND SUSTAINED RECOVERY COULD BE ACHIEVED.
IN A SENSE, THE DIFFICULT ECONOMIC ISSUES WE MUST NOW
ADDRESS ARE IN FACT THE PRICE WE PAY FOR THE VERY SUCCESS OF
OUR POLICIES, AND THE STRENGTH OF THE GROWTH THAT HAS BEEN
ACHIEVED IN THE ECONOMY.
IN ADDRESSING THESE ISSUES WE MUST ACCEPT THAT THE WORLD
DOES NOT OWE US A LIVING. WE CANNOT EXPECT TO RAISE
AUSTRALIA'S LIVING STANDARDS JUST BY CALLING TO AN EVER
GROWING EXTENT ON THE WORLD'S SAVINGS.
AUSTRALIA MUST TO BE PREPARED TO LOOK CLOSELY AT ITS
INDUSTRIAL STRUCTURES AND BE PREPARED TO EMBRACE CHANGES
WHICH WILL INCREASE OUR POTENTIAL TO COMPETE.
WE NEED TO BE PREPARED TO UNDERTAKE THE INVESTMENT NECESSARY
TO LIFT OUR PRODUCTIVITY AND PRODUCE GOODS AND SERVICES OF
THE KIND AND QUALITY WHICH IS DEMANDED IN WORLD TRADE.
INCREASINGLY SUCH DECISIONS ARE LIKELY TO REQUIRE A
WILLINGNESS ON OUR PART TO EXAMINE CLOSELY WHERE OUR
COMPARATIVE ADVANTAGE LIES IN WORLD TRADE, AND TO SEEK TO
SHIFT RESOURCES OUT OF AREAS WHERE OUR ADVANTAGES ARE LEAST
INTO THOSE AREAS WHICH WILL MAXIMIZE OUR CHANCES TO SELL IN
OUR REGION.
AND, NOW AS MUCH AS ANYTIME IN THE PAST THREE YEARS,
AUSTRALIA NEEDS THE SAME HIGH QUALITY OF ECONOMIC
DECISION-MAKING, AND THE SAME COMMITMENT TO FISCAL AND
MONETARY DISCIPLINE, AND THE SAME ACCORD-BASED APPROACH TO
INCOMES POLICY TO ENSURE NON-INFLATIONARY LONG-TERM GROWTH
AS HAS SERVED US SO WELL OVER THE PAST THREE YEARS.
WE WILL-NOT BE DIVERTED FROM OUR TASK OF RESPONSIBLE
MACROECONOMIC MANAGEMENT. OUR INCOMES POLICY HAS BEEN
SECURED FOR A FURTHER TWO YEARS. OUR COMMITMENT TO THE
TRILOGY OF FISCAL RESPONSIBILITY IS FIRM. AND OUR MONETARY
POLICY WILL BE FIRM BUT ACCOMMODATING TO A RATE OF ECONOMIC
GROWTH WHICH IS CONSISTENT WITH LOW INFLATION.
WE WILL CONTINUE TO REMOVE PROGRESSIVELY THE REMAINING
OBSTACLES TO GROWTH AT A PACE WHICH CAN BALANCE THE
COMPETING [ NTERESTS OF THOSE DIRECTLY AFFECTED. 
THERE CAN BE NO DOUBT THAT THE MONTHS IMMEDIATELY AHEAD WILL
CALL FOR CAREFUL, DIFFICULT AND SOMETIMES TOUGH DECISIONS.
THOSE DECISIONS WILL REFLECT OUR CONTINUING COMMITMENT TO
THE ACHIEVEMENT OF SOCIAL PROGRESS, REFORM AND EQUITY
THROUGH SUSTAINABLE ECONOMIC GROWTH. IN THE FINAL ANALYSIS,
THOSE DECISIONS ARE THE ULTIMATE AND INESCAPABLE
RESPONSIBILITY OF THE ELECTED GOVERNMENT OF AUSTRALIA. WE
ACCEPT THAT RESPONSIBILITY UNRESERVEDLY.
YET, JUST AS THE SUCCESS OF THE PAST THREE YEARS COULD NOT
HAVE BEEN ACHIEVED WITHOUT THE WORK AND CO-OPERATION OF ALL
SECTIONS OF THE AUSTRALIAN COMMUNITY, AND JUST AS THOSE
ACHIEVEMENTS ARE, IN A VERY REAL SENSE, THE ACHIEVEMENTS OF
THE AUSTRALIAN PEOPLE, SO IN THE YEARS AHEAD OUR SUCCESS AS
A NATION WILL BE A SHARED RESPONSIBILITY.
SUCCESS IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY GUARANTEED TO ANY NATION, EVEN
ONE SO FUNDAMENTALLY FORTUNATE AS OURS. NOW MORE THAN EVER,
IT IS SOMETHING THAT HAS TO BE WORKED AT AND WORKED FOR,
UNREMITTINGLY NOT ONLY BY GOVERNMENTS, BUT BY THE WHOLE
COMMUNITY. I AM PROUD TO BE AT THE HEAD OF SUCH A GOVERNMENT, AS I AM
IMMENSELY PROUD TO BE AT THE HEAD OF SUCH A PEOPLE AND SUCH
A NATION DURING THESE THREE GREAT YEARS AND THE EVEN
GREATER YEARS OF ACHIEVEMENT FOR AUSTRALIA TO COME.
YET LET ME SAY THIS IN CONCLUSION: THE THREE YEARS DURING
WHICH I HAVE HAD THIS HIGHEST OF PRIVILEGES OF LEADING THIS
GREAT COUNTRY HAVE CONFIRMED, MONTH BY MONTH AND YEAR BY
YEAR, MY DEEPEST CONVICTION THAT IF THE SUCCESS WE ALL SO
DEEPLY DESIRE FOR OUR COUNTRY IS TO BE SECURED FOR THIS AND
FUTURE GENERATIONS, THEN IT WILL BE ONLY UNDER THE
LEADERSHIP OF A LABOR GOVERNMENT, ACTING ON TRUE LABOR
PRINCIPLES IN THE AUTHENTIC LABOR TRADITION. 



CHECK AGAINST DELIVERY EMBARGOED UNTIL DELIVERY
SPEECH BY THE PRIM4E MINISTER
LUNCHEON FOR PRIME MINISTER OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA
CANBERRA 6 MARCH 1986
Prime minister and M~ rs Lho
I recall with pleasure my visit to Seoul a little over two
years ago. I remember the warmth of the hospitality
extended to me on that occasion. I also recall, Prime
Minister, the bracing temperatures in your otherwise
beautiful country in the depths of February.
We had hoped to welcome President Chun Doo-Hwan to
Australia in 1983, when his visit had to be cancelled as a
result of the tragedy of the Rangoon bombing. We look
forward to seeing him in Australia when circumstances
permit. Mr Prime Minister, I have great pleasure in welcoming you
and your delegation here in Canberra and to Australia
today. Korea is a nation with which Australia has had contact over
a long period. The connection goes back at least to the
early days of this century, when Australian missionaries
went to work in your country. Some 18,000 Australian
servicemen fought in the Korean War and more than 250
Australians lost their lives during those hostilities.
After the war the relationship gradually changed as Korea
itself changed. Our political links remain as firm as ever
but, alongside them, the economic relationship has grown
and become increasingly important to both our countries.
Two-way trade has now reached the level of $ 1.6 billion per
annum. In 1984/ 85 the Republic of Korea was our 8th
largest trading partner, compared with our 14th largest in
1980/ 81. During that period trade between our two
countries grew by over 110%. 
2.
Korean exports to Australia of manufactured goods are
approaching annual levels of $ 500 million. They are
welcome to the Australian consumer. They have added to the
range of commodities available on the Australian market and
have enhanced our living standards.
Australia meantime has become a competitive and reliable
supplier of energy and raw materials to Korean industry.
we have also supplied a range of high quality farm products
to your country.
In short, the trading relationship is a mutually beneficial
and complementary one, and there seems no reason why it
should not continue to grow and flourish in the future.
I am aware, of course, of our Korean friends'
dissatisfaction with the imbalance in Australia's favour in
our bilateral trade and of the Korean interest in greater
access to the Australian market.
Concern has also been expressed from the Australian side
about some Korean trading policies which appear to be
restrictive or at odds with the declared objective of
gradually opening the internal market.
It is important for the two sides to work together in a
constructive spirit towards the resolution or management of
these issues. The visit by our Trade Minister, Mr Dawkins,
to Seoul last year was clear evidence of what can be
achieved through this approach to the trade relationship
between both our countries.
Korea and Australia are partners in the Asia-Pacific
region. Australia recognizes Korea's important role and
conspicious efforts directed to achieving economic
co-operation at the inter-Governmental and private sector
levels. In particular, we appreciated Korea chairing the
last meeting of Senior Officers of the Regional Trade
officials. We look forward to the continuation of this
dialogue and to Korea's continued close involvement with
the process.
Australia would like to see a situation where trade flows
continue to expand between our countries. Exports in both
directions have been going up by leaps and bounds, and the
record of the last decade shows that Korean exports have
been increasing considerably faster than those of
Australia. There clearly are ample further opportunities
for both sides to sell a lot more to each other and for
both sides to benefit in consequence.
And it is important to note that the framework for our
trading relations is underpinned by a healthy political
relationship. we share with the Republic of Korea a number
of common political concerns and international perceptions.
we consider ourselves to be one of Korea's reliable friends
and are prepared to play a positive role in helping the
Republic of Korea consolidate its position as an important
actor in the Asia-Pacific region. 
I do not need to rehearse here the dangers and complexities
of the Korean peninsula. Despite these, over the past year
and a half we have witnessed noteworthy contacts and
exchanges between North and South.
Australia naturally supports the contacts at Panmunjom and
elsewhere. We were particularly pleased when last year,
for the first time since the division of the peninsula some
forty years ago, North and South were able to agree on an
exchange of visits of separated family members. It is true
that only in this one area, and then only one time, has
there been tangible progress and that it is, therefore,
necessary to remain cautious in our assessments of where
these contacts will lead. Australia, nevertheless, shares
the hopes of countries of goodwill around the world that
the dialogue will continue.
Clearly, in developing the scope for further negotiations
with the North, it is important that there be continued
stable political development in the South. The pace and
timing will necessarily be determined by Korean realities.
It is nevertheless appropriate for me to record here the
firm belief of the Australian community that a democratic
and pluralistic political system is certain to be a source
P of enduring fundamental national strength. For us, we hold
it as an article of faith that a political system that
inspires political participation and support is not
something which detracts from national security but is
rather a key element of that security. It follows that we
wish the Republic of Korea well in its march toward the
announced goal of political modernisation and full
A democratisation.
Mr Prime Minister, our two countries are both looking
forward to special events in 1988, events which mark the
maturity of our countries. In that year Korea will play
Aihost to the most prestigious international sporting event,
the Olympic Games. We are aware of the great efforts your
country is making in preparations for the Games and
Australians look forw ' ard to participating in them. Before
that time we should exploit opportunities to expand
56 exchanges between our two countries in the areas of sport
and sport administration.
For our part, Australia will be celebrating its
.4 bicentenary. Many major events have been planned, some
involving participation from abroad, and we hope that your
country will be able to participate actively in our
. X celebrations. I conclude by again saying how glad my colleagues and I are
to receive the Prime Minister of the Republic of Korea and
Mrs Lho in Canberra. On your return, Mr Prime Minister, I
should be grateful if you could convey our best wishes to
His Excellency President Chun Doo-Hwan.
I now invite guests to join mec in a toast to Prime Minister
st'. Shinyong Lho and to relations between his country and
Australia.

CHECK AGAINST DELIVERY EM1BARGOED UNTIL DELIVERY
SPEECH BY THE PRIME MINISTER
AUSTRALIA -JAPAN RELATIONS SYMPOSIUM
MARCH 1986 MELBOURNE
I AM DELIGHTED TO RETURN TO ADDRESS THE AUSTRALIA-JAPAN
SYMPOSIUM AND TO WELCOME THE VERY DISTINGUISHED VISITORS
FROM JAPAN WHO ARE HERE AS PARTICIPANTS. IN PARTICULAR, I
WELCOME MR OKAWARA BACK TO AUSTRALIA. AS JAPANESE
AMBASSADOR TO AUSTRALIA SOME YEARS AGO, HE MADE MANY FRIENDS
FOR JAPAN AND WAS A MOST EMINENT ENVOY.
TWO YEARS AGO I HAD THE PLEASURE OF ADDRESSING YOUR CANBERRA
SYMPOSIUM. ON4 THAT OCCASION I REPORTED, AMONG OTHER THINGS,
ON MY FIRST TRIP TO JAPAN AS PRIME MINISTER. ON THIS
OCCASION, I AM ADDRESSING YOU PRIOR TO MY SECOND TRIP TO
JAPAN IN MIAY. IN 1985 PRIME MINISTER NAKASONE VISITED
AUSTRALIA. THESE VISITS AT THE HEAD OF GOVERNMENT LEVEL
DEMONSTRATE CLEARLY THAT THE AUSTRALIA-JAPAN RELATIONSHIP IS
OF GREAT SIGNIFICANCE TO BOTH OUR COUNTRIES.
IN 1984 I SAID THATr OUR RELATIONSHIP WAS AN EVOLVING ONE,
POISED TO MOVE IN NEW DIRECTIONS. NOW, I AM1 ABLE TO REPORT
THAT THIS HAS IN FACT OCCURRED.
DURING THE PAST TWO YEARS WE HAVE BUILT UPON THE
COMPLEMENTARITIES AND THE INTER-DEPENDENCE OF OUR RESPECTIVE
ECONOMIES. NEW AND BENEFICIAL TRADING OPPORTUNITIES HAVE
BEEN FORGED OVER AND ABOVE OUR EXTENSIVE TRADITIONAL TRADE
IN RAW MATERIALS.
THE BASIS OF THE ~ EW TRADING OPPORTUNITIES HAS BEEN THE
DEVELOPMENTS IN INTERNATIONAL FINANCE. A MAJOR POLICY
INITIATIVE OF THE GOVERNMENT HAS BEEN THE FURTHER
LIBERALIZATION OF THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL MARKET AND, IN
PARTICULAR, THE GRANTING IN 1985 OF 16 NEW FOREIGN BANK
LICENCES, OF WHICH 3 WENT TO JAPANESE BANKS. SIMILAR
LIBERALIZATION OF JAPANESE FINANCIAL MARKETS HAS INCLUDED
THE NEGOTIATION OF RECIPROCAL ARRANGEMENTS FOR THE 4 MAJOR
AUSTRALIAN BANKS TO ESTABLISH IN JAPAN. 
GIVEN THAT JAPAN HAS BECO14E THE WORLD'S LARGEST NET EXPORTER
OF CAP'ITAL AND AUSTRALIA'S LARGEST SOURCE OF FOREIGN FUNDS,
THESE FINANCIAL INNOVATIONS SHOULD FURTHER FACILITATE THE
EFFICIENT CHANNELLING OF THESE FUNDS INTO BOTH THE EQUITY
AND SECURITY MARKETS IN AUSTRALIA. THESE RECIPROCAL
ARRANGEMENTS WILL IMPROVE AUSTRALIAN UNDERSTANDING OF THE
FUNCTIONING OF THE JAPANESE DOMESTIC MARKET, ENHANCING
OPPORTUNITIES IN JAPAN FOR AUSTRALIAN EXPORTERS. THIS WILL
BE ESPECIALLY IMPORTANT AT A TIME OF EXPANDING JAPANESE
DOMESTIC DEMAND FOL; LOWING THE DRAMATIC FALL IN OIL PRICES.
AGAIN, WE SHOULD BE ABLE TO DIVERSIFY OUR EXPORTS TO JAPAN
BY INCREASING THE CON4TRIBUTION OF MANUFACTURES AND SERVICES.
INDEED AUSTRALIA IS WELL PLACED TO EXPAND OUR SHARE OF TRADE
IN THESE ITEMS TO JAPAN. REAL UNIT LABOUR COSTS HAVE FALLEN
IN AUSTRALIA BY ABOUT 2 PER CENT IN EACH OF 1983-84 AND
1984-85 AND WE ARE EXPECTING A FURTHER FALL OF THAT ORDER IN
THE CURRENT FINANCIAL YEAR. THIS HAS BEEN ACHIEVED IN THE
CONTEXT OF A SHARP REDUCTION IN INDUSTRIAL DISPUTATION.
ALLOWING ALSO FOR THE 25 PER tENT DEPRECIATION OF THE $ A
SINCE EARLY 1985 AGAINST THE WEIGHTED AVERAGE OF OUR TRADING
PARTNERS, THIS HAS PUT AUSTRALIAN ENTERPRISES IN THEIR BEST
COMPETITIVE POSITION FOR A DECADE AND A HALF. JAPAN, I.
BELIEVE, CAN LOOK TO AUSTRALIA BOTH NOW AND IN THE FUTURE AS
ONE OF THE WORLD'S MOST RELIABLE AND EFFICIENT TRADING
PARTNERS.
AND ON THE JAPANESE SIDE, THE PROGRAM OF MARKET OPENING
MEASURES INITIALLY ANNOUNCED BY PRIME MINISTER NAKASONE LAST
APRIL IS WELCOME AS A SERIOUS EFFORT TO IMPROVE ACCESS FOR
FOREIGN GOODS. WHILE THE MEASURES SHOULD CONTRIBUTE TO
STRENGTHENING THE WORLD TRADING SYSTEM IN THE FACE OF A
MOUNTING PROTECTIONIST TREND, WE HOPE AND EXPECT THAT THEY
WILL ALSO ASSIST THE DIVERSIFICATION OF OUR EXPORTS.
THE AUSTRALIAN GOVERNMENT IS ACTIVELY PROMOTING
DIVERSIFICATION THROUGH THE PROCESS OF RESTRUCTURING OUR
DOMESTIC INDUSTRY AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF A JAPAN MARKET
STRATEGY. AUSTRALIAN AND JAPANESE COMMITTEES ARE
IDENTIFYING AREAS IN WHICH INDUSTRIAL CO-OPERATION CAN BE
EXPANDED BETWIEEN OUR TWO COUNTRIES. IN THESE DELIBERATIONS
AN EMPHASIS IS BEING PLACED ON AREAS WITH THE GREATEST
EXPORT POTENTIAL FOR AUSTRALIA.
NOTWITHSTANDING THESE DEVELOPMENTS, THE GOVERNMENT
RECOGNISES THAT IT IS VITAL FOR AUSTRALIA TO M4AINTAIN OUR
POSITION AS A COMPETITLV1E, RELIABLE SUPPLIER OF TRADITIONAL
PRIMARY PRODUCTS TO THE JAPANESE MARKET. IN THIS REGARD WE
VALUE THE ASSURANCES OF THE JAPANESE GOVERNMENT THAT
PURCHASES OF PRIMARY PRODUCTS WHETHER THEY BE COAL, BEEF
OR OTHER COMMODITIES WILL BE MADE ON A STRICTLY COMMERCIAL
BASIS AND NOT IN RESPONSE TO THIRD COUNTRY BILATERAL
PRESSURES.
ONE OF THE MATTERS I ESPECIALLY WISH TO TALK ABOUT ON MY
VISIT TO JAPAN AND, BEFORE THAT, IN THE UNITED STATES AND
EUROPE IS THE REGIME FOR INTERNATIONAL TRADE IN AGRICULTURAL
PRODUCTS. 
UNFORTUNATELY, AGRICULTURE HAS ALWAYS BEEN EXCLUDED FROM THE
VARIOUS POST-WAR TRADE LIBERALIZATION ROUNDS. FURTHERMORE,
THE GATT RULES ON AGRICULTURE ARE FAR LESS DISCIPLINED ON
THE USE OF SUBSIDIES, ESPECIALLY EXPORT SUBSIDIES, THAN THE
RULES FOR WORLD TRADE IN MANUFACTURES.
IT IS THE GOVERNMENT'S POSITION THAT IF AGRICULTURAL TRADE
IS TO BE PLACED ON A SOUND ECONOMIC FOOTING, IT IS., ESSENTIAL
FOR PROGRESS TO BE MADE FIRSTLY ON THIS CENTRAL ISSUE OF
SUBSIDIES IN THE UPCOMING NEW ROUND OF MULTILATERAL TRADE
NEGOTIATIONS. THIS IS NOT AN ACADEMIC MATTER. IT HAS A
DIRECT BEARING ON AGRICULTURAL PRICES AND PROFITABILITY FOR
ALL EFFICIENT PRODUCERS. AND AUSTRALIANi FARMERS ARE AMONG
THE 1MOST EFFICIENT PRODUCERS IN THE WORLD.
GATT RULES ON AGRICULTURAL SUBSIDIES THEREFORE NEED
SIGNIFICAN4T CHANGES. AUSTRALIA IS STRONGLY OF THE VIEW THAT
A SOLUTION NEEDS TO COMPREHEND A PHASE OUT OF AGRICULTURAL
EXPORT SUBSIDIES OVER AN APPROPRIATE TRANSITIONAL PERIOD TO
BRING THEIR TREATMENT IN LIN~ E WITH THAT APPLICABLE TO
MANUFACTURES TRADE. THIS SHOULD BE COMBINED WITH A
STRENGTHENING OF THE RULES ON OTHER SUBSIDIES, SUCH AS
PRODUCTION SUBSIDIES, TO REQUIRE A COUNTRY USING THEM TO
REMOVE OR REDUCE THEM IF THEY DAMAGE THE TRADING INTEREST OF
OTHERS.
AUSTRALIA HAS CONSISTENTLY ARGUED OVER THE YEARS THAT
ILLEGAL TRADING PRACTICES VOLUNTARY RESTRAINT
ARRANGEMENTS, ORDERLY MARKETING AGREEMENTS, IMPORT
LICENSING, SUBSIDIES AND THE LIKE ARE CAUSING FUNDAMENTAL
DAMAGE AND UNDERMINE THE MULTILATERAL TRADING SYSTEM AND THE
CREDIBILITY OF THE GATT AS A CHIEF REGULATORY BODY OF THAT
SYSTEM. WE WERE THEREFORE ONE OF THE FIRST COUNTRIES TO
WELCOME AND SUPPORT THE LAUNCHING OF A NEW ROUND OF MTNS
PROVIDING THEIR PRIMARY FOCUS WAS ADDRESSING THE PROBLEMS AT
THE ROOT OF CURRENT TRADE DISPUTES NAMELY NON-TARIFF
BARRIERS AND SUBSIDIES, PARTICULARLY AGRICULTURAL EXPORT
SUBSIDIES.
WELL OVER ONE HALF OF WORLD TRADE IN AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS
IS DEPENDENT ON GOVERNMENT SUBSIDIES, CREDITS AND SPECIAL
ARRANGEMENTS. FROM AN AUSTRALIAN PERSPECTIVE, THE CHIEF
PRIORITY FOR THE NEW ROUND IS TO PLACE AGRICULTURAL TRADE ON
A FAIRER, MORE MARKET-ORIENTED BASIS BY BRINGING THE
INTERNATIONAL RULES ON AGRICULTURAL TRADE INTO LINE WITH THE
RULES ON TRADE MANUFACTURERS.
I SUGGESTED IN BANGKOK IN NOVEMBER 1983 THAT COUNTRIES IN
THE WESTERN PACIFIC REGION AND JAPAN OBVIOUSLY IS CENTRAL
IN THIS CONNECTION MIGHT ADOPT A CO-OPERATIVE AND MUTUALLY
SUPPORTIVE APPROACH TO WORKING TOWARD IMPROVEMENTS IN THE
MULTILATERAL TRADING SYSTEM. 
4.
PROGRESS IN THE REGIONAL CONSULTATIONS WHICH HAVE FOLLOWED
THIS SUGGESTION HAS BEEN MOST PLEASING. AT THIS KEY STAGE
IN THE PREPARATORY PROCESS TOWARDS A NEW ROUND WE SEE VALUE
IN THESE CONSULTATIONS BEING MAINTAINED AND STRENGTHENED.
AND WE ARE DETERMIN4ED TO ENSURE THAT THE NEW ROUND ADDRESSES
ISSUES WHICH ARE I1MPORTANT TO THE SMALLER TRADING COUNTRIES
IN THE REGION.
IN THE CONTEXT OF THE CO-OPERATION IN REGIONAL TRADE
MATTERS, THE AUSTRALIAN GOVERNMENT HAS BEEN KEEN TO TAKE
EVERY OPPORTUNITY TO DEVELOP CLOSE CO-OPERATIVE ARRANGEMENTS
WITH OUR PACIFIC NEIGHBOURS. WE WELCOME', FOR EXAMPLE, THE
CO-OPERATIVE RELATIONSHIPS ESTABLISHED IN THE BUSINESS
SPHERE THROUGH ORGAN'ISATIONS LIKE THE PACIFIC BASIN ECONOMIC
COUNCIL AND IN THE RESEARCH PROGRA14S OF THE PACIFIC TRADE
AND DEVELOPMENT CONFERENCE.
WE ARE ALSO PLEASED WITH THE WAY IN WHICH THE PACIFIC
ECONOMIC CO-OPERATION CONFERENCE ( PECC) HAS BEEN ABLE TO
DRAW TOGETHER BUSINESS LEADERS, ACADEMIC RESEARCHERS AND
GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS IN EXPLORING AVENUES' FOR GREATER
ECONOMIC COOPERATION. A NUMBER OF JAPANESE LEADERS IN THESE
FIELDS HAVE MADE VALUABLE CONTRIBUTIONS TOWARDS THIS PROCESS
WHICH BEGAN IN 1980.
IN OUR POLITICAL RELATIONSHIP WITH JAPAN, REGULAR FOREIGN
POLICY CONSULTATION BETWEEN OUR NATIONS IS NOW FIRMLY
ESTABLISHED. IN JUNE LAST YEAR BILL HAYDEN REFERRED IN
TOKYO TO AUSTRALIA'S APPRECIATION OF THE EFFORTS JAPAN HAS
CONTINUED TO MAKE TO ENSURE THIS CONSULTATION OCCURS. HE
ALSO MENTIONED ( AND IN THE PRESENCE OF TWO0 DISTINGUISHED
AMBASSADORS OF JAPAN, ONE PRESENT AND ONE PAST, I ENDORSE
THIS) THE COMPLIMENT AUSTRALIA TAKES FROM THE SENIOR
APPOINTMENTS WHICH ARE MADE HERE BY THE JAPANESE GOVERNMENT.
AS OUR RELATIONSHIP WITH JAPAN HAS GROWN TO MATURITY, WE
HAVE UNDERSTOOD THE VALUE OF REGULAR AND OPEN CONSULTATION.
BEGINNING WITH THE AUSTRALIA-JAPAN MINISTERIAL COMMITTEE,
WHICH MET FOR THE EIGHTH TIME IN 1985, WE HAVE BUILT UP A
FRAMEWORK OF CONSULTATIONS WHICH HAS STOOD FIRM THROUGH
POLITICAL CHANGES AND NEW ECONOMIC CIRCUMSTANCES. WE HAVE
BECOME ACCUSTOMED, AS PARTICIPANTS IN A MATURE RELATIONSHIP
MUST, TO AIRING OUR DIFFERENCES FRANKLY AND SEEKING
SOLUTIONS WHICH ALL CAN ACCEPT.
AT AN OFFICIAL LEVEL, THE RANGE OF OUR CONSULTATIONS IS
WIDENING: A HIGH-LEVEL MEETING ON TRADE IS BEING HELD THIS
WEEK IN TOKYO, TO BE FOLLOWED SHORTLY AFTERWARDS BY THE
EIGHTEENTH IN THE SERIES OF TALKS BETWEEN FOREIGN MINISTRY
OFFICIALS. AT THIS YEAR'S MEETING, IN ADDITION TO SHARING
VIEWS ON ISSUES OF BROAD INTERNATIONAL CONCERN, THE FOCUS OF
ATTENTION WILL ALSO BE ON POLITICAL DEVELOPMENTS IN OUR
REGION, ESPECIALLY IN THE PHILIPPINES. 
AUSTRALIA AND JAPAN HAVE A SHARED INTEREST IN STAnILITY,
ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT AND DEMOCRACY IN THE PHILLIPINES. FOR
OUR PART, WE HAVE INCREASED BY 50% OUR AID COMMITMENT TO THE
PHILLIPINES, AS ANNOUNCED BY THE FOREIGN MINISTER, BILL
HAYDEN, DURING HIS RECENT VISIT TO MANILA. WE HAVE ALSO
INDICATED OUR WILLINGNESS TO CONTRIBUTE TO MULTILATERAL
EFFORTS BY SYMPATHETIC DEVELOPED COUNTRIES TO ASSIST THE
PHILLIPINES IN ITS CURRENT VERY DIFFICULT ECONOMIC
SITUATION. JAPAN AND AUSTRALIA HAVE MUCH TO GAIN FROM THE PRESERVATION
OF PEACE, WHETHER THROUGH THE AUSPICES' OF THE UNITED NATIONS
OR THROUGH STRONG SUPPORT FOR DISARMAM~ ENT INITIATrIVES.
LATER IN THE YEAR, JAPANESE AND AUSTRALIAN OFFICIALS WILL
HOLD SPECIALISED CONSULTATIONS ON DEVELOPMENT ASSISTANCE AND
DISARMAMENT RATTERS. I LOOK FORWARD TO THE OUTCOME OF THOSE
DELIBERATIONS. LADIES AND GENTLEMEN,
THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN AUSTRALIA AND JAPAN IS NOT JUST A
RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN TRADERS AND BETWEEN GOVERNMENTS.
THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN OUR TWO NATIONS HAS BROADENED AND
DEEPENED INTO AREAS BEYOND THE ECONOMIC AND THE POLITICAL.
OVER 3,000 YOUNG JAPANESE HAVE VISITED AUSTRALIA ON WORKING
HOLIDAY VISAS: MANY AUSTRALIANS HAVE ENJOYED A MATCHING
EXPERIENCE IN JAPAN. JAPANESE TOURISTS TO AUSTRALIA HAVE
REACHED THE 100,000 MARK THIS YEAR, AFTER SEVERAL YEARS OF
RAPID GROWTH.
OVER 20,000 AUSTRALIANS A YEAR ARE NOW STUDYING JAPANESE,
AND SOME 19 TERTIARY INSTITUTIONS IN AUSTRALIA
UNIVERSITIES, COLLEGES OF ADVANCED EDUCATION AND THE LIKE
NOW OFFER COURSES IN JAPANESE STUDIES.
AUSTRALIAN ARTS FESTIVALS ARE INTRODUCING BOTH CONTEMPORARY
AND TRADITIONAL JAPANESE CULTURE TO AUSTRALIAN AUDIENCES,
AND THE SPONSORSHIP OF JAPANESE COMPANIES IN AUSTRALIA IS
MAKING AN IMPORTANT CONTRIBUTION4 TO THE EXHIBITIONS,
CONCERTS AND PERFORMANCES WHICH ENRICH THE RELATIONSHIP IN A
WAY THAT IS NO LESS VALUABLE FOR BEING INTANGIBLE.
IN JAPAN, TOO, AUSTRALIA IS MAKING AN IMPACT AS A VIBRANT,
YOUNG COUNTRY WHOSE TALENTED ARTISTS, MUSICIANS, DANCERS,
FILM-MAKERS AND WRIT RS CAN COMPETE WITH ANY INTERNATIONAL
COMPETITORS FOR A PLACE IN THE DYNAMIC JAPANESE ARTS SCENE.
WE WERE PLEASED WITH THE RESPONSE IN OCTOBER LAST YEAR TO
THE FIRST MAJOR EXHIBITION OF AUSTRALIAN 20TH CENTURY ART IN
TOKYO, AND WE HOPE TO FOLLOW IT WITH OTHERS. AUSTRALIAN
STUDIES ARE NOW TAUGHT IN SEVERAL UNIVERSITIES IN JAPAN, AND
THE OPENING THIS YEAR OF THE FIRST FULLY FLEDGED AUSTRALIAN
STUDIES CENTRE, AT NANZAN UNIVERSITY IN NAGOYA, IS A
SIGNIFICANT MIL'ESTONE FOR US. 
THERE IS, AS YOU KNOW, CONSIDERABLE INTEREST IN JAPAN IN THE
CULTURE AND TRADITIONS OF THE AUSTRALIAN ABORIGINAL PEOPLE,
AND SCOPE EXISTS FOR WIDENING THE EXPOSURE IN JAPAN OF THIS
RICH AUSTRALIAN HERITAGE.
IN 1988, THE AUSTRALIAN BICENTENNIAL CELEBRATIONS WILL
INVOLVE THE PEOPLE OF OUR TWO COUNTRIES IN MORE CONCENTRATED
CONTACT THAN AT ANY PREVIOUS TIME.
OUR BICENTENARY IN 1988 -IS ESSENTIALLY A DOMESTIC
CELEBRATION, BUT SUCCESSIVE AUSTRALIAN GOVERNMENTS HAVE ALSO
WANTED TO OFFER OTHER NATIONS THE OPPORTUNITY TO CELEBRATE
WITH US. NO COUNTRY HAS RESPONDED WITHI GREATER ENTHUSIASM
TO OUR INVITATION THAN JAPAN AND THAT GIVES ME AND, I AM
SURE, ALL AUSTRALIANS GREAT PLEASURE.
AT THE INSTIGATION OF FOREIGN MINISTER ABE, A MOST
PRESTIGIOUS GROUP OF PRIVATE SECTOR INDIVIDUALS HAS COME
TOGETHER INI TOKYO TO FORM THE JAPAN AUSTRALIA BICENTENNIAL
COMMITTEE, UNDER THE CHAIRMANSHIP OF A GREAT FRIEND OF
AUSTRALIA, MR EISHIRO SAITO, WHO IS ALSO THE CHAIRMAN OF THE
JAPA?" AUSTRALIA BUSINESS COOPERATION COUNCIL AND THE
CKLtIRMAN OF NIPPON STEEL.
THAT COMMITTEE WILL BE PLANNING AND OVERSEEING THE MANY AND
VARIED FORMS OF JAPANESE PARTICIPATION IN 1988. THEY ARE
CONSIDERING, FOR EXAMPLE, OUR INVITATION TO BE ASSOCIATED
WITH THE NATIONAL BICENTENNIAL SCIENCE CENTRE, AN IMPORTANT
AND LASTING PROJECT FOR 1988.
SUCH A PROJECT HAS A PARTICULAR APPROPRIATENESS FOR JAPAN,
AS ONE OF THE MOST TECHNOLOGICALLY ADVANCED NATIONS IN THE
WORLD. THERE WILL BE MAN\ Y OTHER FORMS OF JAPANESE PARTICIPATION,
ESPECIALLY IN THE TALL SHIPS EVENT, IN EXPO' 88, AND IN THE
ARTS AND ENTERTAINMNET PROGRAM. JAPANESE INVOLVEMENT HAS

WE LOOK FORWARD TO SHARING AND ENJOYING THE VARIED

WHICH THAT SPECIAL YEAkR WILL GENERATE.

EMBARGOED UNTIL DELIVERY CHECK AGAINST DELIVERY
AUSTRALIA: APPROACHING 1988
MELBOURNE 5TH APRIL 1986
MR CHAIRMAN, MR PREMIER, MINISTERS, PARLIAMENTARY
COLLEAGUES, DISTINGUISHED GUESTS, FRIENDS.
FIRST, MR CHAIRMAN, LET ME THANK AND CONGRATULATE THE
VICTORIAN BRANCH FOR BRINGING US TOGETHER, IN THIS VERY
REPRESENTATIVE ASSEMBLY OF VICTORIANS AND AUSTRALIANS, WITH
THE TIMELY THEME OF APPROACHING 1988 THE BICENTENNIAL YEAR
OF THIS NATION.
I SAY ' TIMELY', BECAUSE, WITH THE YEAR ITSELF LESS THAN TWO
YEARS AWAY, AND WITH PLANNING AND ASSOCIATED ACTIVITIES WELL
ADVANCED AT BOTH THE NATIONAL AND STATE LEVELS, THERE IS A
NEED FOR US ALL TO BEGIN TO THINK SERIOUSLY ABOUT THE
MEANING AND PURPOSE OF THIS EVENT ITS MEANING AND PURPOSE
FOR AUSTRALIA AND AUSTRALIA'S FUTURE.
WITHOUT THAT CONTENT OF THOUGHT AND SELF-EXAMINATION, THE
CELEBRATIONS THEMSELVES, HOWEVER MEMORABLE I HOPE AND
BELIEVE THEY WILL BE FOR ALL AUSTRALIANS, WOULD BE HARDLY OF
MORE SIGNIFICANCE TO AUSTRALIA THAN THE VISITATION OF
HALLEY'S COMET SOMETHING WORTH SEEING OF COURSE, AND
SIGNIFICANT IN ITSELF BUT ESSENTIALLY IRRELEVANT TO OUR
COUNTRY'S FUTURE.
AND NOW IS THE TIME WELL BEFORE THE DAWN OF 1988 TO
BEGIN THAT PROCESS OF NATIONAL STOCK-TAKING WHERE WE HAVE
BEEN AND) WHERE WE ARE GOING SO THAT BY THE BICENTENNIAL
YEAR THERE WILL HAVE EMERGED A CLEARER UNDERSTANDING, BY ALL
AUSTRALIANS, OF THE MEANING AND TRUE SPIRIT OF THE
BICENTENARY. MUCH OF THAT MEANING AND SPIRIT IS I BELIEVE, ENCAPSULATED
IN THE THEME NOW ESTABLISHED FOR THE BICENTENNIAL.
ONE OF THE EARLIEST DECISIONS I TOOK ON BECOMING PRIME
MINISTER THREE YEARS AGO WAS TO CHANGE THE DESIGNATED THEME.
YOU MAY REMEMBER THAT UNDER THE PREVIOUS DISPENSATION IT HAD
BEEN DESIGNATED AS " TWO HUNDRED YEARS OF AUSTRALIAN
ACHIEVEMENT". I HAD ALWAYS THOUGHT THAT INAPPROPRIATE NOT
BECAUSE OF ANY LACK OF LEGITIMATE PRIDE IN WHAT WE HAVE 
ACHIEVED ( QUITE THE CONTRARY), BUT BECAUSE, IN MY VIEW AND
IN MY COLLEAGUES' VIEW, IT WAS PAR TOO NARROW AND INDEED
BACKWARD-LOOKING, A FOCUS.
SO AT MY SUGGESTION, ON AUSTRALIA DAY 1984, THE BICENTENNIAL
AUTHORITY ESTABLISHED A NEW THEME OR TO BE MORE CORRECT
REVERTED TO ITS ORIGINALLY PREFERRED THEME " AUSTRALIANS
LIVING TOGETHER".
AND I THINK THE REALLY IMPORTANT POINT TO NOTE IS THAT THIS
REPRESENTS MUCH MORE THAN A STATEMENT ABOUT AUSTRALIA AS IT
HAS GROWN OVER THE LAST 200 YEARS. IT IS THAT, BUT MUCH
MORE. IT IS AN AFFIRMATION FOR THE FUTURE.
BECAUSE, OUR CAPACITY TO LIVE TOGETHER, TO WORK TOGETHER IN
OUR INCREASINGLY DIVERSE SOCIETY, IN A GENUINELY
MULTICULTURAL SOCIETY, IS THE VERY CONDITION FOR OUR FUTURE
SUCCESS AND SURVIVAL AS A COHESIVE COMMUNITY.
SO THE BICENTENNIAL THEME, " LIVING TOGETHER" IS NOT JUST A
DESCRIPTION OF MODERN AUSTRALIA IN 1988 BUT, IN A VERY REAL
SENSE, A PRESCRIPTION FOR AUSTRALIA FAR BEYOND 1988.
AND I BELIEVE THAT THE AUSTRALIAN ACHIEVEMENT OVER THE LAST
3 YEARS HAS PROVIDED AN OUTSTANDING EXAMPLE OF THAT
PRESCRIPTION IN ACTION.
MY FRIENDS, IT IS EXACTLY 3 YEARS NEXT WEEK SINCE THE
HISTORIC NATIONAL ECONOMIC SUMMIT.
BEHIND THE CONCEPT OF THE CONFERENCE LAY MY LONG-HELD BELIEF
THAT AUSTRALIA COULD NO LONGER AFFORD TO GO DOWN THE PATH OF
CONFRONTATION AND FRAGMENTATION WHICH HAD EMBITTERED AND
DISFIGURED SO MANY ASPECTS OF OUR NATIONAL LIFE, FOR MUCH OF
THE PREVIOUS DECADE.
AND I SAID WHEN OPENING THE SUMMIT ON 11 APRIL 1983 THAT THE
NEED FOR NATIONAL RECONCILIATION WENT FAR BEYOND THE
ECONOMIC CRISIS WE THEN FACED AND NEED I REMIND YOU THAT
AUSTRALIA WAS THEN EXPERIENCING ITS WORST ECONOMIC CRISIS
FOR 50 YEARS.
I SAID THEN THAT WHAT WAS AT STAKE WAS NOT ONLY THE URGENT
AND IMMEDIATE TASK OF ACHIEVING ECONOMIC RECOVERY, BUT THE
FOUNDATIONS WE COULD LAY FOR THE WHOLE FUTURE OF THIS GREAT
COUNTRY OF OURS INTO THE 21ST CENTURY.
YOU WILL RECALL THAT THERE WAS A GREAT DEAL OF SCEPTICISM
AND CYNICISM ABOUT OUR APPROACH, AT THE TIME AND IT WAS
NOT CONFINED TO THE RANKS OF OUR POLITICAL OPPONENTS, WHO OF
COURSE HAD A DEEP VESTED INTEREST AS THEY STILL HAVE IN
THE FAILURE OF OUR APPROACH.
IN SOME QUARTERS, THE WHOLE THING FROM THE CONCEPT OF THE
SUMMIT TO THE SPECIFIC PROPOSALS WHICH EMERGED FROM THE
COMMUNIQUE AND THE ACCORD WAS DISMISSED AS MERE RHETORIC
SOMETHING THAT COULD NOT WORK, SOMETHING THAT COULD NOT
LAST. 
LET ME SAY THIS: IF THE IDEA OF NATIONAL RECONCILIATION AS
THE PRECONDITION FOR NATIONAL RECOVERY AND NATIONAL
RECONSTRUCTION WAS MERE RHETORIC, THEN IT SPEAKS VOLUMES FOR
THE PRACTICAL POWER OF RHETORIC IN THE ECONOMIC, INDUSTRIAL
AND SOCIAL LIFE OF THIS NATION.
BUT OF COURSE, IT WAS NOT RHETORIC AT ALL. THE WORDS, THE
APPROACH, THE CONCEPT CLOTHED CLEAR AND PRACTICAL PROPOSALS,
AND EFFECTIVE MACHINERY, FOR THE ATTAINMENT OF OUR NATIONAL
ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL GOALS AND OBJECTIVES.
AND I EMPHASISE THE TWIN NATURE OF THE GOALS THE SOCIAL
GOALS HAND IN HAND WITH THE ECONOMIC GOALS; SUSTAINED AND
SUSTAINABLE ECONOMIC GROWTH AS THE MEANS TO OUR WIDER SOCIAL
ENDS AND OBJECTIVES OF A FAIRER, MORE EQUITABLE SOCIETY.
WHO COULD NOW DISMISS AS RHETORIC AN APPROACH THROUGH WHICH
MORE THAN 600,000 JOBS HAVE BEEN CREATED WITHIN 3 YEARS?
AN APPROACH WHICH HAS REDUCED INDUSTRIAL DISPUTATION TO
ITS LOWEST LEVEL FOR 16 YEARS;
AN APPROACH WHICH HAS RESTORED THE PROFIT SHARE AND
REDUCED REAL UNIT LABOUR COSTS TO THE LEVELS OF THE LATE
1960' S AND EARLY 19701S;
AN APPROACH WHICH HAS RESTORED AUSTRALIA'S INTERNTAIONAL
COMPETITIVENESS TO THE LEVELS OF 15 YEARS AGO; AND
AN APPROACH WHICH HAS CREATED THROUGHOUT THE COMMUNITY A
NEW AWARENESS AND ACCEPTANCE OF THE NEED FOR FUNDAMENTAL
RESTRUCTURING OF KEY SECTORS OF THE AUSTRALIAN ECONOMY.
THESE ARE THE ESSENTIAL ELEMENTS OF THE ECONOMIC RECORD OF
THE PAST 3 YEARS.
BUT WHAT IS EVEN MORE IMPORTANT NOW, AS WE APPROACH 1988,
AND AS WE PLAN FAR BEYOND 1988, IS THE CAPACITY OF OUR
APPROACH TO MEET THE DEMANDS OF THE FUTURE.
THE PRICES AND INCOMES ACCORD IS OF COURSE THE. CENTRAL PART
OF OUR APPROACH THE KEYSTONE OF THE ARCH.
BUT THE ACCORD ITSELF IS PART OF A COMPREHENSIVE APPROACH TO
DECISION MAKING.
IT PLAYED A CRUCIAL ROLE THOUGH BY NO MEANS AN EXCLUSIVE
ROLE IN THE REMARKABLE ACHIEVEMENT OF STRONG GROWTH
WITHOUT INCREASED INFLATION. IT WILL CONTINUE TO PLAY THAT
ROLE. BUT THE SUBSTANTIAL IMPORTANCE OF THE ACCORD NOW LIES
IN ITS CAPACITY TO PROVIDE A FRAMEWORK OF CERTAINTY AND
PREDICTABILITY, YET AT THE SAME TIME TO PROVIDE A
FLEXIBILITY TO COPE WITH UNFORSEEN CHANGES IN ECONOMIC
CIRCUMSTANCES. THIS IS WHY IT IS IMPERATIVE THAT THE ACCORD SHOULD BE
MAINTAINED. 
YET WE NOW KNOW THAT OUR POLITICAL ADVERSARIES PROPOSE TO
STRIKE AT THE VERY HEART OF THE ACCORD AND UNDERMINE THE
FOUNDATIONS UPON WHICH ALL THAT HAS BEEN ACHIEVED SO FAR HAS
BEEN BUILT.
I MUST SAY I FIND IT ALL VERY FASCINATING.
THE POLICY MAKING PROCESSES OF THE LIBERAL PARTY ARE NOW
QUITE REMARKABLE. THESE DAYS, IT APPEARS, THEY DECIDE HOW
TO MARKET A POLICY BEFORE THEY MAKE THE POLICY.
PERHAPS SOMEWHERE IN THE INNER RECESSES OF THE LIBERAL PARTY
SECRETARIAT I SUPPOSE WE CAN CALL THEM THE " FACELESS
MEN" THERE IS A DOCUMENT CONTAINING THE LIBERAL WAGES
POLICY. BUT THE PARLIAMENTARY LIBERAL PARTY HAS YET TO BE
INFORMED. MR VALDER HAS YET TO TELL THEM NOT ONLY HOW TO
VOTE, BUT WHAT THEY ARE SUPPOSED TO BE VOTING ON. NO DOUBT
THE POLICY WILL BE LEAKED IN DUE COURSE.
BUT AT PRESENT THEY HAVE NO POLICY.
YET THEY DO HAVE, AS YOU NOW KNOW, A STRATEGY TO MARKET
THEIR NON-EXISTENT POLICY.
YOU HAVE ALL BEEN WARNED.
YOU ARE TO BE NEUTRALISED!
SERIOUSLY LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, WHAT AN EXTRAORDINARY
BUSINESS IT ALL IS!
NO POLICY, NO PROPOSAL, NO PLAN BUT A MARKETING STRATEGY.
AND, THIS, FROM THE ONCE GREAT LIBERAL PARTY THE PARTY OF
MENZIES, THE PARTY EVEN OF BOLTE.
I MIGHT SAY IN PASSING THAT I CAN UNDERSTAND FROM A CERTAIN
BIZARRE INCIDENT THIS WEEK, HOW SIR HENRY BOLTE MUST HAVE
FELT WHEN THE FINANCIAL REVIEW, A MONTH OR SO AGO HEADLINED
AN EDITORIAL " SIR HENRY BOLTE TURNS IN HIS GRAVE".
BUT THE EDITORIAL DEALT COMPREHENSIVELY WITH THE APPALLING
DECLINE IN STANDARDS AND CAPACITY OF THE LIBERAL PARTY AND
THEREFORE WAS IN ALL OTHER RESPECTS COMPLETELY ACCURATE.
BUT WHILE WE STILL AWAIT IN BREATHLESS EXPECTATION, I AM
SURE THE ANNOUNCEMENT OF THE LIBERAL WAGES POLICY, WE KNOW
ONLY TOO WELL WHAT IT REALLY MEANS.
WHATEVER ITS FINAL FORM, ITS MEANING AND PURPOSE WOULD BE
RETURN TO THE CONFRONTATIONISM OF THE 1970' S AND ALL THAT
THAT PRODUCED.
SO WHAT EMERGES WITH CRYSTAL CLARITY, LADIES AND GENTLEMEN,
THE ALTERNATIVE IS NO ALTERNATIVE AT ALL. NEITHER IN TERMS
OF MEN OR IN TERMS OF MEASURES. 
I DO NOT DISGUISE, FOR A MOMENT, THAT WE FACE, AS A
GOVERNMENT AND AS A NATION, A TIME OF DIFFICULT AND COMPLEX
DECISION MAKING.
I DO NOT DISGUISE THAT SOME OF THESE DECISIONS MAY BE
UNPALATABLE UNPALATABLE TO MAKE, UNPALATABLE FOR SOME OF
US TO TAKE.
BUT THE IMPORTANT THING FOR US, FOR AUSTRALIA AND FOR THE
LABOR GOVERNMENTS OF AUSTRALIA, FOR THE AUSTRALIAN LABOR
PARTY, FOR THE AUSTRALIAN LABOR MOVEMENT AND FOR THE WHOLE
AUSTRA LIAN COMMUNITY IS THAT THE CRUCIAL DECISIONS ARE
MADE WITHIN A COHERENT AND CONSISTENT FRAMEWORK, WORKING
TOWARDS COHERENT AND CONSISTENT ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL
OBJECTIVES. A COHERENT FRAMEWORK AND A CLEAR COMMITMENT TO
LONG-TERM GOALS ALONE CAN ENSURE THAT THE DECISIONS, HOWEVER
DIFFICULT, ARE THE CORRECT DECISIONS.
WE HAVE ESTABLISHED THAT FRAMEWORK. WE ARE COMMITTED
IRREVOCABLY TO THOSE GOALS AND OBJECTIVES THE ECONOMIC AND
SOCIAL OBJECTIVES OF THE AUSTRALIAN LABOR PARTY AND THE
AUSTRALIAN LABOR GOVERNMENT.
AND IN CONTINUING THE WORK OF ACHIEVING OUR GOALS, I BELIEVE
THAT THE SPIRIT OF CO-OPERATION BETWEEN ALL SECTIONS OF THE
COMMUNITY, WHICH HAS BEEN AT THE HEART OF SO MUCH THAT HAS
BEEN ACHIEVED DURING THE PAST 3 YEARS, WILL BE JUST AS
IMPORTANT AND NECESSARY, IN THE YEARS TO 1988 AND BEYOND.
THERE IS NO WAY AHEAD AT LEAST NO VIABLE WAY AHEAD FOR
AUSTRALIA BY ANY REVIVAL OF THE CONFRONTATION AND
FRAGMENTATION OF THE PAST, OR BY THE PURSUIT OF PURELY
SECTIONAL SHORT-TERM INTERESTS.
LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, A VITAL ASPECT OF THE PROCESS OF
CO-OPERATION AND CONSULTATION WE HAVE ESTABLISHED OVER THE
LAST 3 YEARS HAS BEEN THE CO-OPERATION BETWEEN OUR LABOR
GOVERNMENTS THROUGHOUT AUSTRALIA.
MR PREMIER, I CONGRATULATE YOU AND YOUR MINISTERIAL AND
PARLIAMENTARY COLLEAGUES ON THIS 4TH ANNIVERSARY OF YOUR
ELECTION AND ON A MAGNIFICENT RECORD OF ACHIEVEMENT FOR THE
ADVANCEMENT OF LABOR'S CAUSE IN VICTORIA AND IN AUSTRALIA.
I SHOULD MENTION HERE THAT TOMORROW NIGHT THE PREMIER WILL
JOIN ME IN LAUNCHING THE NATIONAL DRUG OFFENSIVE A PROGRAM
FOR A COMPREHENSIVE AND RELENTLESS CAMPAIGN AGAINST THE
ILLEGAL DRUG TRAFFIC IN AUSTRALIA. THIS IS A MATTER OF
PROFOUND IMPORTANCE TO OUR FUTURE AND OUR CHILDRENS'
FUTURE AND ONE WHICH, OF COURSE, UTTERLY TRANSCENDS ANY
POLITICAL OR REGIONAL CONSIDERATIONS. AND I ACKNOWLEDGE THE
WHOLEHEARTED SUPPORT AND CO-OPERATION WE ARE RECEIVING FROM
ALL STATE GOVERNMENTS IN THIS GREAT NATIONAL EFFORT.
BUT, AS MUCH AS THE IN THE WIDER ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL ISSUES
OF OUR TIME, THE SUCCESS OF THAT EFFORT REQUIRES, IN THE
FINAL ANALYSIS, THE CO-OPERATION AND SUPPORT OF THE WHOLE
COMMUNITY. 
6
IT NEEDS THE VERY KIND OF COMMUNITY CO-OPERATION SUPPORT AND
GOOD WILL WHICH BROUGHT US OUT OF THE ECONOMIC CRISIS AFTER
MARCH 1983 AND WHICH WE STILL NEED AS A NATION TO ENSURE
THAT OUR EFFORTS ARE AS EFFECTIVE IN THE FUTURE, AND TO
ENSURE THAT THOSE EFFORTS ARE NOT DISSIPATED IN SECTIONAL
POINT SCORING.
I HAVE SAID MANY TIMES, AND I SAY AGAIN TO THIS
REPRESENTATIVE ASSEMBLY, THERE IS NO AUTOMATIC GUARANTEE OF
SUCCESS FOR NATIONS OR-FOR THAT MATTER, POLITICAL
PARTIES IN OUR HIGHLY COMPETITIVE AND CHALLENGING WORLD.
WE MAY DESERVE SUCCESS BUT WE CANNOT COMMAND IT. IT HAS TO
BE WORKED FOR, AND WORKED AT, UNREMITTINGLY.
AND I BELIEVE THAT NOW, AS MUCH AS AT ANY TIME IN THE PAST
THREE YEARS, THE KEY TO ALL WE HOPE FOR, ALL WE STRIVE FOR,
IS THE MAINTENANCE AND FOSTERING OF THE SPIRIT AND FACT OF
NATIONAL RECONCILIATION AND NATIONAL CO-OPERATION.
I AM CONVINCED THAT THAT SPIRIT OF CO-OPERATION IS THE
NECESSARY FOUNDATION FOR THE SUCCESS WE ALL SO DEEPLY DESIRE
FOR OUR COUNTRY, AND FOR THE CONTINUED SUCCESS OF WHAT IS
NOW A UNIQUELY AUSTRALIAN EXPERIENCE AND A UNIQUELY
AUSTRALIAN EXPERIMENT. IT IS ACKNOWLEDGED THROUGHOUT THE
WORLD TO HAVE BEEN A REMARKABLE SUCCESS IN THE PAST THREE
YEARS. THE TASK AHEAD IS TO BUILD ON THAT SUCCESS, IN
ADVANCING AND ENHANCING THE EXPERIENCE AND EXPERIMENT OF A
GENUINELY MULTICULTURAL NATION PERHAPS, IN-THAT RESPECT
THE MOST DIVERSE ON EARTH LIVING TOGETHER, WORKING
TOGETHER, BUILDING TOGETHER AN EVEN FAIRER, MORE SECURE AND
MORE EQUITABLE SOCIETY IN THIS GREAT COUNTRY OF OURS. 



PRIME MINISTER
EMBARGOED UNTIL DELIVERY CHECK AGAINST DELIVERY
AUSTRALIAN MADE PHASE II LAUNCH
GREENSBOROUGH 7 APRIL 1986
Last June, when I announced tha Australian Made Campaign I
was confident it would be a success.
I was confident that Australians were waiting for a campaign
like this and were prepared to do their bit for the country
by choosing Australian made products where they represented
value for money.
But I am pleased to say that my high hopes for the campaign
have been well and truly exceeded.
Because the message conveyed by the ' True Blue'
advertisements is really getting through to the Australian
buying public.
And the green and gold ' Australian Made, logo is being
attached to more and more products, showing that they are
genuine, true blue, Australian made goods.
Since the campaign began, more than 800 manufacturers have
signed up for the right to display that green and gold logo.
In using the logo, those manufacturers are tellin~ you, the
customers, that their product is the genuine Auss e article.
It's even more encouraging that a number of manufacturers
have boosted their local content so that they can qualify
for the logo.
And it's not just manufacturers, but shoppers themselves,
who have seen the benefits of supporting Australian made
products. They're not just saying " Yes, I know about the True Blue
advertisement but I'm not going to do anything about it".
The fact is more and more Australians are now buying
Australian made products and in doing this they are
playing a central role in helping Australia meet the
economic challenge it faces.
The collapse in many of our export prices means that the
world has cut Australia's income to the tune of $ 1500 per
Australian family. Australian workers and families and
businesses have to practise restraint and work together if
we are to build a better Australia for ourselves and our
kids. 
2
By choosing products bearing the official green and gold
logo, you are helping your country by reducing our
dependence on imports and by boosting Australian companies,
Australian jobs, Australian products.
if, in a single year, shoppers were to switch $ 200 of their
purchases per family member from imported to Australian Made
products, we would cut about $ 2.5 billion off Australia's
import bill. And that would be a very significant step
indeed on the way to building prosperity for the future.
The success of the Australian Made-camnpaign so far has
spurred the Government on to a second phase, and that's what
I'm here to launch today at Greensborough Shopping Centre.
During this second phase we'll be aiming to boost the
quality of a broader range of Australian made products.
we'll also be encouraging more manufacturers to use the
green and gold logo. We'll be helping retailers mount
Australian made promotions like the one displayed here at
Greensborough this week. And, of course, we will be running
True Blue advertisements on TV and in regional newspapers.
what we are seeking to do is to have more products on the
shelves of our shops and supermarkets bearing the green and
gold logo,. so that more Australian made products will be
bought by shoppers, and so that the quantity of imported
goods we need will fall.
I want to congratulate the Advance Australia Foundation for
its great work in organising the campaign. I want to
congratulate Australian manufacturers and retailers for
getting Aussie products on the shelves.
But most of all I want to congratulate you, the Australian
shopper, for choosing Australian made products where they
represent value for morley.
You are helping your fellow Australians by keeping them
secure in their jobs, you are helping your country trade its
way out of its difficulties, and you are helping your
children by building a stronger economy.
You have ev. ery right to be proud of yourselves, and I thank
you.

SPEECH BY THE PRIME MINISTER
FOR PRIME MINISTER LEE KUAN YEW
PARLIAMENTARY LUNCH 15 APRIL 1986
PRIME MINISTER LEE
I AM DELIGHTED TO HAVE YOU WITH US IN AUSTRALIA AGAIN. OVER
THE YEARS YOU HAVE BEEN A FREQUENT VISITOR HERE AND, WHILE I
HOPE THAT YOU HAVE ALWAYS FELT VERY WELCOME, I THINK THAT
YOU WILL HAVE NOTED IN YOUR CONTACTS WITH AUSTRALIANS A
STEADILY INCREASING WARMTH AND INTEREST TOWARDS SINGAPORE
AND TOWARDS EAST AND SOUTH EAST ASIA GENERALLY.
WHEN I REFLECT UPON AUSTRALIAN PERCEPTIONS OF ASIA TODAY I
SEE VAST AND WELCOME DIFFERENCES COMPARED WITH 20 YEARS AGO.
AT THAT TIME MANY AUSTRALIANS VIEWED OUR REGION AS TROUBLED,
EVEN THREATENING. THE INTRINSIC CAPABILITIES OF THE PEOPLES
OF ASIA FOR ENTERPRISE, SOUND ADMINISTRATION, ADAPTATION AND
CO-OPERATION WERE UNDERRATED. BUT THAT IS TRUE NO MORE
BECAUSE AUSTRALIANS HAVE WITNESSED THE FLOURISHING OF ALL
THESE THINGS OVER THE PAST TWO DECADES.
WHEN AUSTRALIANS THINK OF ASIA NOW THEY DO NOT THINK OF A
REGION ENTIRELY PROBLEM FREE NO REGION AND NO NATION,
AUSTRALIA INCLUDED, IS THAT. BUT WE THINK OF ADMIRABLE AND
IN SOME CASES TRULY REMARKABLE ECONOMIC GROWTH PERFORMANCES,
THE EFFECTIVE COMBINING OF TECHNOLOGICAL MODERNISATION WITH
EXISTING CULTURAL TRADITIONS, EXAMPLES OF MAJOR POLICY
TRANSFORMATIONS, AS IN CHINA, AND GREAT ACHIEVEMENTS IN
BUILDING INSTITUTIONS FOR REGIONAL CO-OPERATION, NOTABLY
ASEAN. PRIME MINISTER, YOU HAVE BEEN ONE OF THE FOREMOST LEADERS IN
THIS PROCESS OF FUNDAMENTAL AND BENEFICIAL CHANGE WHICH WE
HAVE WATCHED UNFOLD IN ASIA. YOU HAVE PRESIDED OVER TWO
DECADES OF STRONG ECONOMIC GROWTH. TAKING AS A STARTING
POINT SINGAPORE'S CENTRAL ROLE AS AN ENTREPOT AND A
TRANSPORT AND COMMUNICATIONS HUB IT HAS BECOME AN ECONOMIC
METROPOLIS FOR ALL OF SOUTH EAST ASIA. 
THIS PERFORMANCE BY YOUR COUNTRY HAS BEEN PART OF THE WIDER
PHENOMENON OF THE SURGE AHEAD OF THE SO CALLED NEWLY
INDUSTRIALISED COUNTRIES. THIS, IN COMBINATION WITH THE
EARLIER ASCENDANCY OF JAPAN TO THE STATUS OF A MAJOR GLOBAL
AND REGIONAL ECONOMIC FORCE, HAS MADE THE PACIFIC RIM THE
AREA OF GREATEST ECONOMIC DYNAMISM IN THE WORLD IN RECENT
TIMES. THROUGH THE SAME PERIOD AS THESE CHANGES WERE OCCURRING IN
ASIA, AUSTRALIANS WERE STEADILY COMING TO TERMS WITH A NEW
AND DIFFERENT WORLD, A WORLD IN WHICH OUR INTERESTS BECAME
CLOSELY INTERWOVEN WITH THE COUNTRIES OF OUR REGION.
THE SIGNIFICANCE TO AUSTRALIA OF ASIA AND THE PACIFIC HAD
ALREADY BECOME APPARENT IN STRATEGIC AND SECURITY TERMS
BEFORE IT WAS APPARENT IN ECONOMIC TERMS. THE DRAMATIC
ECONOMIC CHANGE FOR US CAME WITH THE IMPACT ON OUR TRADE
PATTERNS OF TWO DEVELOPMENTS. THE FIRST WAS THE RAPID
ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT OF JAPAN. THE SECOND WAS THE ENTRY OF
BRITAIN INTO THE EUROPEAN COMMUNITY, A GROUPING WHOSE
POLICIES HAVE SUBSEQUENTLY HAD SIGNIFICANT IMPACT ON
TRADITIONAL AUSTRALIAN EXPORTS.
THE FIRST OF THESE CHANGES LED TO JAPAN BECOMING AUSTRALIA'S
MAJOR TRADING PARTNER AND THE SECOND TO THE DISINTEGRATION
OF OUR PREDOMINANTLY AGRICULTURAL EXPORTS TO EUROPE AND,
MORE RECENTLY, TO COMPETITION IN THIRD MARKETS FROM HEAVILY
SUBSIDISED AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS. THE MAJOR RE-ORIENTATION
IN OUR TRADE PATTERNS, TOGETHER WITH THE SHIFT TO THE
PACIFIC BASIN AS THE MAJOR CENTRE OF TRADE AND ECONOMIC
GROWTH, HAS CHANGED THE FUNDAMENTALS OF AUSTRALIA'S
INTERNATIONAL RELATIONSHIPS.
HOWEVER IT IS NOT ENOUGH SIMPLY TO RECOGNISE THAT THE
INEVITABLE REALITY OF OUR GEOGRAPHY, AND AUTONOMOUS ECONOMIC
FORCES IN THE OUTSIDE WORLD, HAVE WORKED TOGETHER TO MAKE IT
NECESSARY FOR AUSTRALIA TO FOCUS ON ASIA AND THE PACIFIC IN
THE CLOSING DECADES OF THIS CENTURY. THAT CONJURES UP TOO
PASSIVE AND DETERMINISTIC A PICTURE. I WANT TO SAY INSTEAD
THAT WE WILL BE AN ENTHUSIASTIC PLAYER IN THE ECONOMICS OF
THE REGION, EMBRACING THE OPPORTUNITIES WHICH OUR
ADVANTAGEOUS GEOGRAPHICAL POSITION OPENS UP, AND RELISHING
THE PROSPECT OF CLOSER INVOLVEMENT WITH PACIFIC RIM ECONOMIC
GROWTH. TO ACCOMPLISH THIS IS PARTLY A MATTER OF OUR ADOPTING
APPROPRIATE POLICIES IN AUSTRALIA ITSELF. MY GOVERNMENT IS
PLACING CONSIDERABLE EMPHASIS ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF A MORE
DYNAMIC AND INTERNATIONALLY COMPETITIVE INDUSTRIAL BASE.
THIS IS REFLECTED IN OUR APPROACH TO INDUSTRY RESTRUCTURING
AND THE MOVEMENT TO LOWER LEVELS OF PROTECTION. THE
AUSTRALIAN STEEL AND CAR INDUSTRY PLANS, AND THE EXTENSIVE
MOVES MADE TO LOWER INDUSTRIAL PROTECTION TO MINIMUM LEVELS
ON COMPUTERS AND OTHER HIGH TECHNOLOGY ITEMS ITEMS OF KEEN
EXPORT INTEREST TO COUNTRIES SUCH AS SINGAPORE HAVE
TOGETHER SECURED A QUALITATIVE CHANGE IN AUSTRALIA'S IMPORT
REGIME. THESE POLICIES WILL CONTRIBUTE TO OUR ABILITY TO
INCREASE OUR TRADE WITHIN THE REGION AS BOTH AN EFFECIENT
AND COMPETITIVE SUPPLIER OF AUSTRALIAN PRODUCTS AND AS A
MARKET FOR GOODS FROM OUR NEIGHBOURS. 
WHILE AUSTRALIA AND SINGAPORE WILL BOTH BENEFIT UNILATERALLY
FROM THE DEVELOPMENT OF OUR REGION WE SHOULD ALSO BE ALIVE
TO OPPORTUNITIES WHERE THE BUSINESS INTERESTS OF BOTH OUR
COUNTRIES COULD GAIN FROM WORKING TOGETHER TO SECURE JOINT
VENTURE PROJECTS OR INCREASED MARKET OPPORTUNITIES. OUR
RESPECTIVE INTEREST IN THE POSSIBILITIES ASSOCIATED WITH A
NEW, DYNAMIC CHINA SEEMS PARTICULARLY SUGGESTIVE OF SUCH
CO-OPERATIVE APPROACHES.
TO NOTE THE VITALITY OF PACIFIC RIM ECONOMIES IS NOT TO DENY
OR IGNORE CURRENT PROBLEMS AND THE NEW CHALLENGES THEY POSE.
THE INTERNATIONAL ECONOMIC ENVIRONMENT IN WHICH THE REGION
MUST OPERATE IS NOT AN EASY ONE. POOR COMMODITY PRICES, FOR
EXAMPLE, ARE TAKING A TOLL ON SOME OF THE MAJOR ASIAN
ECONOMIES AS THEY ARE ON AUSTRALIA. I AM AWARE, PRIME
MINISTER, THAT SINGAPORE'S VIRTUALLY UNSURPASSED RUN OF
ECONOMIC GROWTH HAS SLOWED. YOUR GOVERNMENT HAS EMBARKED
UPON A SUBSTANTIAL RE-EVALUATION OF ITS ECONOMIC POLICIES
WITH A VIEW TO RESTRUCTURING AND RE-ESTABLISHING THE
CONDITIONS FOR GROWTH. SINGAPORE IS NOT ALONE IN FACING
THAT KIND OF PROBLEM BUT YOU ARE DOING IT WITH
CHARACTERISTIC DETERMINATION AND PURPOSEFULNESS.
BUT CLEARLY NO AMOUNT OF SOMETIMES PAINFUL BUT ESSENTIAL
ADJUSTMENT IN THE DOMESTIC ECONOMIC POLICIES OF SINGAPORE,
AUSTRALIA OR ANY. OTHER COUNTRY WILL BE EFFECTIVE IF IT IS
STYMIED BY TRENDS IN THE INTERNATIONAL TRADING ENVIRONMENT
WHICH ARE HOSTILE TO GROWTH. AUSTRALIA AND SINGAPORE SHARE
A COMMON CONCERN ABOUT DEVELOPMENTS WE HAVE OBSERVED IN THE
INTERNATIONAL TRADING SYSTEM OVER RECENT TIMES. TRENDS
TOWARDS PROTECTIONISM AND BILATERALISM ULTIMATELY ARE TO THE
DETRIMENT OF ALL TRADING NATIONS.
DURING MY FORTHCOMING VISIT TO THE UNITED STATES AND EUROPE
I WILL SEEK TO IMPRESS AUSTRALIA'S CONCERNS WITH
PROTECTIONIST TRENDS AND TO HIGHLIGHT THE EXTREME IMPORTANCE
TO ALL COUNTRIES OF ENSURING THE COMMENCEMENT OF AN
EFFECTIVE AND BALANCED ROUND OF MULITLATERAL TRADE
NEGOTIATIONS. AUSTRALIA ATTACHES PARTICULAR IMPORTANCE TO THE ISSUE OF
SUBSIDIES ON AGRICULTURAL EXPORTS. AUSTRALIA'S INTERESTS IN
THE NEW ROUND NEVERTHELESS EXTEND BEYOND THE AGRICULTURAL
QUESTIONS. WE ALSO CONSIDER IT ESSENTIAL THAT PROGRESS BE
MADE ON OTHER MATTERS OF MUTUAL INTEREST TO SINGAPORE AND
AUSTRALIA. THESE INCLUDE VOLUNTARY RESTRAINT ARRANGEMENTS,
LICENSING ARRANGEMENTS, PRODUCT STANDARDS AND TRADE IN
SERVICES. I AM VERY PLEASED WITH THE RESPONSE OF COUNTRIES IN THE
REGION TO MY PROPOSAL THAT WE JOINTLY EXPLORE THE SCOPE FOR
CO-OPERATION IN ORDER TO MAXIMISE OUR REGION'S INFLUENCE ON
THE NEW ROUND OF MULTILATERAL TRADE NEGOTIATIONS. IN
PARTICULAR I WISH TO RECORD MY APPRECIATION OF THE STRONG
SUPPORT THAT SINGAPORE HAS PROVIDED TO THIS PROCESS.
VALUABLE PROGRESS HAS BEEN MADE IN IDENTIFYING AND
DEVELOPING SHARED PERCEPTIONS IN THE PREPARATION FOR THE NEW
MTN ROUND.
